This document emphasizes the revolutionary potential of AI, which combines the current development and new trends to open previous treatment and better results of patients.

articleTitle: Intelligent Dengue Prediction and Management: a Companied-Optimized Ensemble Approach With Advanced Feature Selection and Dynamic Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Dengue fever poses a significant health challenge, necessitating efficient resource allocation. Complex internal and external factors contribute to non-linear fluctuations in dengue fever occurrences, making resource planning challenging. While machine learning (ML), as well as deep learning (DL) algorithms, are pivotal in healthcare analysis, there's a need for enhanced predictive capabilities and intelligent recommendations. This research aims to execute an advanced early-warning system for dengue fever forecasting, emphasizing improved prediction accuracy and refined recommendation strategies. In data pre-processing phase, techniques like outlier removal as well as missing data imputation have been employed to elevate data quality. To optimize feature selection, we introduce an Advanced Neighbour Count-based Dragonfly Electric Fish Optimization (ANC-DEFO) algorithm. This method aims to determine most relevant features for accurate dengue fever prediction. Subsequently, selected features undergo an Optimized Ensemble Classifier (OEC), leveraging a combination of “Convolutional Neural Network, Artificial Neural Network, and Support Vector Machine” based on their high-ranking performance. Beyond prediction, our model contributes to public health by offering tailored medical recommendations in areas where dengue fever is predicted. Recommendations span precautionary measures, immunity-boosting remedies, drug prescriptions, and strategies for minimizing disease spread. The research evaluates the model against various comparative algorithms, demonstrating its efficiency and superiority in early dengue fever diagnosis.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of ML Models on Google App Store Data with Imbalanced Classes
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of four machine learning models-Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM-in classifying imbalanced app store data. The dataset, characterized by a class imbalance, underwent preprocessing with SMOTE to enhance minority class representation. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Logistic Regression underperformed, achieving an accuracy of 59%. Random Forest improved to 76%, while XGBoost and LightGBM demonstrated superior performance with accuracies of 78%, achieving a better balance between precision and recall for the minority class. An ANOVA test confirmed statistically significant differences in model accuracy (F-statistic: 366.20, p-value: 5.98e-15). ROC analysis further highlighted XGBoost and LightGBM as the most effective models, achieving the highest AUC of 0.78. XGBoost and LightGBM are recommended for imbalanced classification tasks, offering both accuracy and balanced performance.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Field Equipment Design based on High-Performance Heterogeneous Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: At present, high performance equipment is gaining importance due to the computational capabilities it allows to develop, they are present in workstations as well as in personal computers. In field work it is important to analyze large volumes of data, as well as the use of applications that require high computational capacity, which the high performance solutions described above cannot be used, due to the need for energy, which in field work is not always available as energy sources are not always available. In the present work we describe a design of a low cost system to work in the field, based on Nvidia portable architecture, coupled with a parallel processing system based on Neuro Stick 2, for portability is coupled to the system a touch screen, a battery system to power the system and expansion units, as a result of the design we present the results of the operation of the system, The design can be applied and scaled, depending on the needs and works, taking into account that the Linux operating system and the programs to be used must be compatible.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence-Based Student Computational Thinking Analysis Model (AI-SCTAM) for Curriculum Development
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Computational thinking (CT) has been widely used to improve students' comprehension of mathematical and scientific subjects. However, there is a scarcity of information available regarding the challenges faced by students and the development of their conceptual knowledge in these learning environments, particularly in relation to the integrated curriculum. There is a need to help with course-level curriculum development to improve teaching and learning. Hence, this paper proposes an artificial intelligence-based student computational thinking analysis model (AI-SCTAM) to predict student engagement in learning and improve curriculum development. This research attempted to determine the association between student engagement measures using the machine learning (ML) method to determine the degrees of student involvement. The ML divides students into two groups: highly engaged and poorly engaged, according to the criteria used to measure their degree of involvement. The findings of the correlation study showed a positive association between engagement measures and performance. Analyzing the relationship between student engagement and performance will guide the development of course materials and activities. STEM education metrics based on engagement levels will be proposed to personalize students' learning experiences.

articleTitle: Crypto Trading Platform: MERN Stack with Real-Time Data and Social Features
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The increasing complexity of cryptocurrency markets necessitates the development of efficient portfolio management tools that provide real-time tracking, price updates, and market awareness. This paper focuses on an advanced concept of a cryptocurrency wallet service provision that provides a summary of available coins, their prices, available quantities, and customers‘ transaction histories. Developed for the ‘frontend’ using React.js and for the ‘backend’ using Node.js, which uses the CoinGecko API for receiving live market prices and collecting curated news blog articles from other APIs. The data related to the wallets are efficiently managed since the application is built based on the MongoDB schema, and in addition to this, the user authentication is also integrated. A responsive design of the user interface allows for showing both a portfolio summary and the latest news related to cryptocurrencies, thus suggesting an ‘everything in one place’ solution for users interested in cryptocurrencies. This system shows how real-time data integration could be implemented, how the system is friendly to users, and how the system manages the content. This system could be expanded in the future with predictive analytics and an AI recommendation system for the portfolio management and contents.

articleTitle: AI Surveillance Security System with Blockchain Storage and Alerts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The increasing demand for enhanced security systems highlights the need for advanced solutions capable of detecting human activities such as thefts, fights, stealing, and violence in real-time. Traditional surveillance systems often fall short due to their reliance on manual monitoring, basic anomaly detection techniques, and insecure data storage mechanisms. This project proposes a comprehensive system leveraging YOLO (You Only Look Once), a state-of-the-art object detection framework, to identify and classify abnormal human activities from both recorded videos and live footage. To ensure secure data handling, blockchain technology is integrated, providing tamper-proof storage and robust privacy measures. In the event of extreme activities, the system is equipped to send automated email alerts to owners or emergency services, facilitating timely interventions. The proposed system addresses limitations of existing methods by offering real-time detection, multi-model integration for complex activity recognition, and secure, scalable data management. This innovative approach aims to enhance security measures, reduce response times, and create a reliable framework for preventing and managing critical incidents.

articleTitle: MediVault DApp: A Electronic Health Record Application Using Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The healthcare industry stands to benefit greatly from blockchain technology due to its robust security, privacy protection, confidentiality, and decentralized nature. This study outlines how blockchain can revolutionize current medical data systems and proposes a framework for its implementation. The primary objective of this framework is to ensure secure storage of electronic records by establishing comprehensive access protocols for users. When patients seek medical care, hospitals generate and store patient records in a decentralized application (DApp), which is a blockchain- based platform for maintaining electronic medical records. Medical professionals can modify patient records, while patients can retrieve their medical information from the DApp using public keys. Electronic Health Records (EHRs) allow healthcare providers to monitor information necessary for compliance with insurance companies and government regulations. EHRs serve as a centralized data repository for storing doctors' orders related to laboratory tests, x-rays, and other diagnostic procedures. The proposed system aims to optimize individual medical information management, minimize redundant testing, reduce treatment delays, and equip patients with adequate information to make informed decisions.

articleTitle: Advancing 3D Face Morphing Detection Via Synthetic Data and Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Face morphing attacks have posed great threats to the security of biometrics by mixing face features with the intention of passing identity verifications. In this regard, most of the current detection methods usually exhibit poor generalization to real variations due to limited data diversity. This work proposes a new deep learning framework for detecting attacks involving 3D face morphing, leveraging the advantages of geometric facial modeling for the generation of high-quality diverse synthetic 3D datasets with adversarial generative models. This is achieved by detecting morphing inconsistencies with the use of spatial and texture-level artifacts, allowing domain adaptation for robust performance of the solution across synthetic-real scenarios. Experimental results confirm its superior accuracy, adaptability to unseen techniques, and robustness against pose, lighting, and occlusion variations, thus turning out to be an efficient solution in biometric security.

articleTitle: Analysis of Automation in Foundries for Transforming Production Efficiency, Quality Control, and Operational Resilience
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The foundry industry, a cornerstone of manufacturing, has undergone significant transformations due to the integration of automation technologies. This survey paper examines the evolution of automation in foundries, exploring its historical development, key adoption drivers, and the ongoing challenges faced by traditional operations. Technological advancements driving this change include the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and cyber-physical systems (CPS), such as digital twins. Through case studies, the paper illustrates practical implementations of these technologies, such as IoT-enabled monitoring, robotics in core making and molding, AI-driven defect detection, and CPS integration in smart foundries. The advantages of automation are emphasized, including increased productivity, improved quality control, energy efficiency, sustainability, and enhanced workplace safety. Despite these benefits, the adoption of automation faces significant hurdles, such as high initial investment costs, integration with legacy systems, skill gaps, and cybersecurity concerns. The paper also identifies future trends, including the rise of collaborative robotics (cobots), edge computing, 5G technologies, and the vision for fully autonomous foundries. This comprehensive survey offers valuable insights into the current state of foundry automation, its transformative potential, and future directions for researchers and industry stakeholders seeking to leverage these advancements for operational excellence.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Powered Edge Analytics for IoT-based Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The rapid expansion of loT-based sensor networks has necessitated the development of efficient edge analytics frameworks to process vast amounts of data in real time while minimizing computational overhead. Deep learning-powered edge computing has emerged as a transformative approach, enhancing data processing capabilities at the network edge while addressing constraints related to latency, bandwidth, and energy consumption. This study introduces a novel algorithm, Lightweight AI Model Compression for Energy-Efficient IoT Edge Devices (LiteEdgeAI), designed to optimize deep learning models for resource-constrained edge environments. The proposed method employs quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation techniques to achieve significant reductions in model size and computational complexity while maintaining high inference accuracy. To validate the efficiency of LiteEdgeAI, a comparative simulation analysis was conducted against existing state-of-the-art algorithms using key performance metrics such prediction accuracy, energy efficiency and computational complexity. Experimental results demonstrated that LiteEdgeAI outperformed baseline models. The findings highlight the potential of LiteEdgeAI in enabling scalable, low-power, and real-time edge intelligence for IoT-based sensor networks.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning and Domain Adaptation in Hyperspectral Image Processing: an Overview
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Fine-tuning a pre-trained model is a type of transfer learning: a pre-trained model that works on a large dataset is transferred onto a particular task or a smaller dataset, such as a hyperspectral image. The efficacy of such a technique is most visible in hyperspectral imaging since the data is usually too high-dimensional with a very scarce number of available annotated datasets. By using the pre-trained model, fine-tuning enables spatial and spectral features to be captured with lower computational overheads than fully training models. Domain adaptation approaches, including feature alignment and adversarial training, are also adapted to overcome limitations caused by the domain shift phenomenon due to the variability of the sensor, environmental changes, and temporal changes. Hyperspectral imaging is applied in diverse fields, including agriculture, environmental monitoring, mineral exploration, defense, medical diagnostics, and food quality assessment. Such applications are unique in the sense that HSI can integrate spatial and spectral information to achieve detailed material analysis. Advanced learning techniques will enhance the effectiveness of HSI models in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Survey on DL - Driven Multi-Modal Data in Cardiovascular Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: One of the primary reasons of illness and mortality across the world is cardiovascular disease (CVD), for the timely detection of which the need for accurate detection methods persists. The last years have seen the development of cutting aged multimodal machine learning methods to enhance diagnosis accuracy that consider multiple types of data. In such scenarios, Phonocardiogram (PCG) signals and Electrocardiogram (ECG) images form integrated data. This review presents the summary of recent research works published on heart abnormality detection models based on a multimodal dataset by combining PCG and ECG data. The PCG signals capture acoustic heart information, including murmurs and other mechanical abnormalities, while ECG images documentation of the heart's electrical functions, aiding in the identification of arrhythmias and other rhythm-related issues. We delve into the various deep learning architectures used in implementing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and process of attention in a complementary way to extract and combine features within these modalities. Building on the insights gained from existing literature in heart abnormality detection using multimodal datasets, we suggest a hybrid deep learning model that effectively integrates ECG pictures and PCG signals. This approach leverages the complementary nature of the two modalities to enhance detection accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: An Iterative Analysis of Deep Learning Models Including LSTM and CNN-GRU for Real-Time Seizure Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Epilepsy is the most common of all neurological conditions, affecting over 50 million people in the global population. Timely prediction of seizures may reduce mortality rates and improve outcomes for affected patients. The existing seizure detection and prediction methodologies rely on machine learning algorithms that need handcrafted features, have poor adaptability to EEG signals, and inadequate generalization capability. Additionally, past reviews have primarily focused on isolated aspects of seizure prediction and not on the comprehensive evaluation of the advancement in DL models along with their integration with the emergent technologies like IoT and transfer learning. The current review bridges this gap by providing an empirical analysis of 15 state-of-the-art DL methodologies for real-time seizure prediction. Some techniques addressed include LSTM, CNN-GRU-AM-based models because they can extract spatiotemporal features automatically and hybrid optimization frameworks such as WCA-PSO-EELM that result in more accurate classifications. New ideas include adaptation for concept drift and transfer learning for adaptability to different patients and lower computations. The review is made on multimodal approaches by integrating EEG and MRI data with IoMT applications for remote monitoring regarding the aspects of accessibility and cost-effectiveness of healthcare. This work is presented, reporting that models such as CNN-GRU-AM and WCA-PSO-EELM offer superior accuracy (>99%) and specificity, while the transfer learning approach proves to be a robust solution to data-scarce scenarios. This review provides a roadmap for future research and clinical deployment by systematically comparing these methods using performance metrics. The results are of significant relevance for personalized medicine, advancing real-time monitoring systems, and developing AI-driven innovations in neurological healthcare sets.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis on Cervical Cancer Detection Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Among the many cancers that afflict females, cervical cancer ranks high. Thousands of women are diagnosed with cervical cancer each year. Early detection of abnormal precancerous tumours helps to prevent cervical cancer. In a cervical cell picture including thousands of cells, the presence or absence of abnormal nuclei is determined by the precise diagnosis made by the clinician or pathologist. In this survey paper analyze 32 research papers regarding the cervical cancer with comparative analysis. In this survey analyzed the importance of cervical cancer prediction and machine learning oriented papers also analyzed. As a result of pathologists and clinicians must rely on a quick and exact detection approach. Conventional detection systems typically consist of two essential processes: segmentation and classification. Eventually, the abnormal sets undergo a final diagnostic search. Computerassisted cervical cancer screening technologies have evolved dramatically in recent years. Correct cell segmentation is critical for the efficacy of a cervical cell screening approach the existing methods are Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) were discussed with diagnose of cervical cancer.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey on NLP-based Approaches for Summarizing Lengthy Research Papers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This work reviews recent advances in NLP-based methods for automatic text summarization, with a focus on how they might be used to summarize lengthy research publications. In light of the exponential rise of textual material, systems that can generate succinct and insightful summaries must be developed to enhance information retrieval and lessen the strain of manual reading. It will review techniques that include extractive summary, in which key phrases are removed from the source text, and abstractive summarizing, where the main concepts are formed into new sentences. It contains some excellent techniques, including graph-based approaches, transformer models (BERT, GPT, and T5), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and hybrid models. Managing domain-specific terminology, maintaining coherence for longer articles, and obtaining computationally effective summarization are some special challenges Metrics of evaluation comprise ROUGE, BLEU, and F1 score. This survey intends to provide a more comprehensive review of present approaches, identify research gaps, and outline possible directions towards the future in order to accelerate the field of artificial text summarization

articleTitle: Next-Gen IDS: Advanced AI for Real-Time Threat Detection in Smart Multiple Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)

authors.preferredName: M N V V K Pavan Kumar
authors.firstName: M N V V K Pavan

abstract: The fast growth of IoT devices brings new security challenges that require a next-generation Intrusion Detection System (Next-Gen-IDS), which can detect real-time information security threats. Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions are a viable candidate to address the shortcomings of conventional IDS; however, the performance of these solutions will largely depend on the nature and volume of the data collected in smart IoT environments, which are often dynamic and heterogeneous. This paper analyzes the integration of AI methodologies like Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) to improve the accuracy, efficiency, and adaptability of IDS in IoT networks. In this work, the types of attacks are detected and classified by a Next-GEN AI IDS. An innovative combination of anomaly detection, behavior analysis, and finding malicious patterns is utilized to detect and mitigate cyber adversaries with negligible latency. The proposed approach is the combination of a pre-trained model Adaptive Recurrent Neural Network (A-RNN) to find the attack patterns effectively and transforms these patterns to the proposed approach Stacked Long Short-Term Memory (S-LSTM) - Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for effective classification of attacks. The strength of the proposed approach applied on two real time datasets such as BETH Dataset, and IoT −23 Dataset are used for experimental analysis. Finally, the proposed approach obtains superior results compared with the existing models.

articleTitle: An Improved Detection of Skin Melanoma Using Hybrid CNN-MobileNet V2 Approach with Multi-Scale Attention
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Identifying melanoma in dermoscopic images is an immense challenge due to the varied appearances of the lesions. This research introduces a hybrid CNN-LSTM model augmented with a multi-scale attention mechanism to tackle this complexity, utilising CNNs for spatial feature extraction and LSTMs for temporal pattern recognition. Our model surpasses traditional CNN and MobileNet V2-LSTM models, with an accuracy of 96.98%, a recall of 96.65%, a specificity of 97.56%, and a JSI of 95.78<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. These measurements demonstrate enhanced sensitivity and reliability compared to baseline models, signifying strong diagnostic capabilities. This study improves melanoma detection, aiding in more precise diagnoses for clinical environments and remote telemedicine applications. Future initiatives involve enhancing the model for more comprehensive skin lesion categorisation.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using EfficientNetB5 and ResNet50 Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a severe diabetes-related eye complication that can result in blindness if left untreated, progressively damages retinal blood vessels with varying degrees of severity. Traditional screening methods predominantly rely on manual expert evaluation, which can be time-intensive, prone to human error, and subject to interpretation variability due to inconsistent image quality. To address these challenges, our research presents an innovative hybrid deep learning solution that seamlessly combines EfficientNetB5 and ResNet50 architectures for automated DR classification. This advanced model strategically harnesses EfficientNetB5 superior feature extraction capabilities alongside ResNet50 sophisticated deep layer processing power to accurately classify DR into mild, moderate, severe, and proliferative stages. Through extensive training on a comprehensive dataset of retinal fundus images, our hybrid approach demonstrates significant improvements in early detection accuracy, reduced diagnostic inconsistency, and enhanced reliability compared to conventional methods. The results validate that this integrated approach provides healthcare professionals with a robust, efficient, and reliable automated screening tool for clinical applications, ultimately addressing the current limitations in DR diagnosis and management while potentially improving patient outcomes through earlier intervention.

articleTitle: Low-Power MIPS32 Processor Design with Cache Implementation Using Clock Gating Techniques on FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a low-power MIPS32 processor with an integrated cache system, leveraging clock gating techniques to optimize power efficiency on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). Clock gating is employed to reduce dynamic power consumption by selectively disabling the clock signal in inactive functional units, thereby minimizing unnecessary switching activity. The proposed architecture incorporates an optimized cache memory hierarchy to enhance performance while maintaining energy efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate significant reductions in power consumption without compromising processing speed., making this design well-suited for power-constrained applications such as embedded systems and IoT devices.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Recognition of Bacterial Brain Abscesses: A Comprehensive Approach Towards Brain Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research paper focuses on developing an advanced deep learning-based framework for the automated detection of brain abscesses disease, a severe condition characterized by the accumulation of pus in the brain tissue due to bacterial infections. This study analyzes MRI images with exceptional precision using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), specifically the DenseNet-121 architecture. By training the model on a diverse and well-curated dataset, the proposed system results in a significant improvement in accuracy, achieving an average accuracy of 95% detection rate, surpassing the performance of models such as ResNet-50 and InceptionV3, which achieved an average of 80% accuracy. This model can accurately identify and delineate abscess regions, eliminating the need for manual intervention. Rigorous evaluations confirm its reliability in differentiating between healthy and infected brain tissues. The findings underscore the potential of this automated approach to expedite diagnosis, enhance clinical decision-making, and improve patient outcomes by facilitating timely intervention in the management of brain abscesses.

articleTitle: Raspberry-Pi Based Semi-Autonomous Rover for Pre-Defined Navigation Path
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The Chandrayaan missions aim to study nearby Moon's composition, mineralogy, geologic evolution. Chandrayaan-1 and Chandrayaan-2 missions had their unique challenges and limitations. India's first lunar mission was Chandrayaan-1, it was launched in cognizant, 2008. and did not include a rover; instead, it carried an orbiter and an impact probe. Success was achieved in the detection of water molecules on the Moon, but in the project that spanned over ten months of operation, the orbiter had to suffer from failure due to overheating and communication problems. Launched in 2019, the Chandrayaan-2 mission included the Pragyan rover, planned for exploring the lunar surface. Unfortunately, the Vikram lander suffered considerable damage during descent from software and trajectory errors, putting the entire mission at jeopardy. The successful soft landing of Chandrayaan-3, India's third lunar research project, in 2023 at the Moon's South Pole drove a momentous turning point for the nation's space exploration endeavors and yielded vital new information for lunar science. To this end, we have developed a semi-autonomous rover that employs the A* path finding algorithm to navigate in a grid-like environment. The major aim, therefore, is for the rover to autonomously plan the best route while avoiding obstacles that were specified in advance. After setting the locations of the rover's source and destination, the current system uses the A* algorithm to find the most efficient path in a grid-like representation. Real-time modifications of its trajectory allow the rover to circumvent obstacles and navigate accurately and safely in an ever-changing environment. Test results show the ability of the rover to perform tasks related to navigation, thus proving the applicability of the A* algorithm in real-life situations such as industrial automation, rescue operations, and autonomous exploration in confined spaces.

articleTitle: Random Forest and Gradient Boosting for Superior Intrusion Detection and Anomaly Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research introduces a novel methodology to improve predictive performance in the domain of intrusion detection and anomaly detection, with a focus on real-world cybersecurity applications. The proposed approach combines advanced data preprocessing, feature selection, and an ensemble learning technique, resulting in a robust predictive model. The core innovation lies in the development of the Boosted Forest model, a hybrid of Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, which optimizes prediction accuracy by leveraging the strengths of both algorithms. The preprocessing phase includes handling missing values, addressing class imbalance using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), and removing outliers with the Inter Quartile Range (IQR) method, ensuring a balanced and noise-free dataset for model training. To enhance model efficiency, the Chi-Square (X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) Test is used for feature selection, allowing for the identification of the most relevant features that influence the target variable. The Boosted Forest model then iteratively refines predictions, improving the accuracy and generalization of the model for complex cybersecurity data. The model's performance is evaluated through key metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. This methodology provides a significant advancement in intrusion detection and anomaly detection, offering improved accuracy, fairness, and applicability for real-world cybersecurity challenges. The proposed framework is a valuable contribution to the detection of security breaches and malicious activities in network environments.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection: Integrating Dual-Staged Attention and Squirrel Search Optimization for Enhanced Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The rapid development of computer networks, such as the internet, has caused a sea change in the ways in which people communicate and share information. The advent of widespread computer networks like the internet has caused a sea change in traditional modes of communication and information sharing. On the other hand, this technical progress has also opened the door for malicious actors to take advantage of loopholes and steal sensitive information, disrupt operations, etc. Therefore, intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are essential for screening harmful traffic and warding off frequent attacks. These algorithms used to work by comparing current attacks to those of the past or by following a predetermined set of rules. But now that data and computing power are more accessible than ever before, machine learning seems to be the way to go. In this study, to present DSAM-CGLSTM, a dual-staged attention mechanism based on conversion-gated Long Short Term Memory network, to capture both short-term mutation and long-term dependence info in the study dataset. To enhance the network's capacity to retrieve the short-term mutation information, hyperbolic tangent functions are incorporated into the input-gate and forget-gate of LSTM. Additionally, the network incorporates a dual-staged attention mechanism, which encompasses both input attention and temporal attention. Consequently, a novel algorithm for optimising the parameters of DSAM-CGLSTM, SSA, has been suggested in this research, which is based on metaheuristics. to use a single Jupyter notebook in the Google Colaboratory environment to conduct the entire experiment. to imported and then implemented the necessary software packages, including seaborn, pandas, matplotlib, keras, besides Tensor Flow, and to used the CICIDS 2017 dataset. During the model's training and validation processes, accuracy and loss were taken into account as performance indicators. With a 98.85% accuracy score, the deep learning model performed quite well when tested on the CICIDS 2017 dataset for attack prediction.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging in Smart Grids with Renewable Energy Sources Using the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Sustainable energy management (EM) advances through integrating electric vehicles (EVs) with smart grids and renewable energy sources (RESs). Traditional optimization strategies face hurdles because EV charging is dynamic while preventing grid congestion remains essential. This paper proposes the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA), a novel approach for optimizing EV charging in SGs integrated with RESs. The primary goals of the proposed method are to minimize energy costs, balance grid load, and accommodate user preferences. SBOA is applied to optimize the EV charging schedules within SGs, with the method implemented and tested on the MATLAB platform. Performance comparisons are made against established optimization techniques, including the Modified Snake Optimization Algorithm (MSOA), Efficient Black Widow Optimization Algorithm (EBWOA), Deep Neural Networks (DNN), and Multi-Objective Robust Optimization (MRO). The results indicate that SBOA significantly outperforms the other methods in terms of energy efficiency and grid stability, achieving a cost of energy (COE) of $136/kWh. These findings underscore the potential of SBOA as an effective tool for optimizing EV charging in SGs with renewable energy (RE) integration.

articleTitle: Smart Car Technology: Computational and Characterization Techniques in Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Smart vehicles represent a significant advancement in automotive technology, integrating various intelligent systems to enhance driving experience and safety. These vehicles utilize advanced circuit boards, microprocessors, and Internet of Things (IoT) features to interact with other vehicles, their environment, and human operators. The study of input and output channels for user interaction in smart vehicles can benefit from queuing analysis to streamline how users interact with the vehicle's systems. This includes optimizing the response times of user commands and interactions with the vehicle's interfaces. By applying queuing theory, the study aims to improve the efficiency of smart vehicle systems, from manufacturing to operational performance, ensuring that smart vehicles deliver on their promise of enhanced functionality, safety, and user experience.

articleTitle: Red Panda Optimization Technique for Voltage Control and Electric Vehicle Reactive Power Management in Smart Micro Grids
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The integration of Electric Vehicles (EV) with Smart Micro Grids (SMGs) is supposed to perform an effective voltage control and active reactive power management for the sake of securing the solidity of the system. Managing current ripple in interleaved boost converters finally is a constant design or control challenge, demanding approaches that allow the performance to be sustained against the load and input variations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid approach for voltage control and EV reactive power management in smart MGs, optimizing grid stability and energy efficiency. The proposed method integrates the Red Panda Optimization (RPO). The aim is to improve the economic performance of the MG integrated with EVs by minimize the Mean Absolute Error (MAE). RPO is utilized to optimize the controller parameters for enhancing voltage control in smart MGs. By then, the suggested method is implemented on MATLAB platform and evaluated with various existing approaches such as Spider Monkey Optimization (SMO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Stochastic Multi Objective Optimization (SMOO), and Hunting Prey Optimization Algorithm (HPOA). The proposed RPO method achieves the MAE at 0.021, demonstrating a significant improvement in voltage control and reactive power management efficiency in SMGs compared to other optimization methods

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection Developments: Analysis of Deep Learning and Hybrid Model Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Brain Tumor detection remains a difficult task in Medical Imaging. Recent developments in deep learning techniques, mainly Convolutional Neural Networks and hybrid models have significantly enhanced the correctness and competence of Tumor classification, segmentation and detection. This study presents a complete review of leading-edge studies focused on Brain Tumor detection with an emphasis on deep learning models and hybrid methodologies. The review includes a variety of approaches such as convolutional neural network (CNN), Capsule Networks, Generative Adversarial Networks, hybrid Convolutional Neural Network - Support Vector Machine (CNN-SVM) and Convolutional Neural Network, and RNN stands for Recurrent Neural Network(CNN-RNN) models. These techniques have demonstrated remarkable success in overcoming challenges such as data scarcity, computational complexity and multi-class Tumor classification. In addition to discussing the methodologies employed in these models, their advantages, limitations and detection accuracy are analysed. Finally, we highlight the emerging trends in AI -based Tumor detection and provide directions for future research aimed at improving diagnostic performance and clinical applicability.

articleTitle: Similarity-Navigated Graph Neural Network-Based Fraud Detection in Credit Card Transactions Optimized with the Greylag Goose Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: People are making daily purchases and sales through the internet, and most of them require them to use their credit cards. Besides making things easier for the customer, this heightens the probability of online credit card frauds. Credit card fraud detection has increased in several nations in the recent past due to the increased incidence of fraud that requires it to become even more of a security issue than before. In this paper, a new deep-learning-based approach for credit card fraud detection is proposed. It is based on the preprocessing stage, hybrid feature selection, and classification stage. In the first instance, the proposed method is used on the Credit Card Fraud Detection (CCF) data set. A prescreening step that uses Z-score Min-Max normalization is applied to ensure that the ranges of each data set are the same. The Crayfish Optimization Algorithm (COA) and the Emperor Penguin Optimizer (EPO) are integrated and used to identify the better attributes. Next, a similarity-navigated graph neural network (SNGNN) is utilized for classification so that the fraudulent transactions and the transactions that are not fraudulent can be differentiated easily. The overall system is also enhanced with Greylag Goose Optimization (GGO) that maximizes the chances of detection. The proposed method achieves a high accuracy in detecting fraudulent transactions, which means the proposed process has virtually limitless potential to speed up the entire process. Thus, high effectiveness is proved by the 99% accuracy rate of the suggested method. This exceptional outcome proves the robustness of the approach and its ability to adapt to various patterns of dependence and data changes.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient SpMM Kernels for GATs and GCNs on a CGLA
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown excellent performance in various fields, such as atomic structure estimation, chemical reaction modeling, and information retrieval aids in Large Language Models (LLMs). Among GNN models, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) and Graph Attention Networks (GATs) are widely applied due to their computational efficiency and scalability. GATs provide higher inference accuracy through the Attention mechanism. Despite their advantages, these models face a significant bottleneck in Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (S <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>MM). Current SpMM platforms, which include potent CPUs, GPUs, and existing hardware accelerators, struggle to balance high performance and low power consumption, making them unsuitable for low-power graph applications. To address these challenges, we propose S <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>MM kernels that leverages the Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Array (CGRA)-based accelera-tor IMAX3 (In-Memory Accelerator eXtension 3). Since the data flow in IMAX3 is static, padding is required to align the number of nonzero elements in each row, increasing data volume. To minimize this overhead, we introduced a new data format with minimal padding and optimized instruction mapping for seamless operations on IMAX3. We estimated the performance when converted to an ASIC using TSMC's 28nm process libraries. The results show that IMAX3 achieves a significant improvement in energy-delay product (EDP), outperforming the CPU i9-10940X by factors ranging from 20.24 x to 1,334.12x, the GPU RTX3090 by up to 1.54x, and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin by up to 172.31x. Compared to prior accelerator work, our kernel delivers EDP improvements ranging from 46.71x to 3,542.76x. These results highlight the exceptional efficiency and scalability of the proposed IMAX3-based SpMM kernel in overcoming GNN bottlenecks.

articleTitle: Attribute Driven News Classification and Analysis System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Innovative approaches to assessing and advancing peace are required due to the growing complexity of international conflicts and social discontent. The Attribute Driven News Classification and Analysis System, an automated system for evaluating and rating peace-related characteristics in news stories, is presented in this research. To determine if an item is in line with positive indications (peace, respect, unity, trust, and justice) or negative ones (conflict, disrespect, chaos, distrust, and injustice), this system classifies articles into predefined labels. Utilizing cutting-edge Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods, this system uses Hugging Face transformers for zero-shot categorization, allowing for accurate and efficient labelling without requiring a lot of user annotations. Selenium-based web scraping is used to gather data in real time, guaranteeing dynamic insights into changing narratives. The system helps users track trends and assess societal harmony by combining preprocessing and reliable scoring algorithms to calculate a comprehensive peace index. The goal of this project is to improve instruments for measuring peace and provide useful information to scholars, politicians, and peacebuilding groups. This System aims to transform the way peace is assessed and advanced by offering a scalable, flexible, and data-driven solution.

articleTitle: Harnessing Big Data in Biotechnology: A Machine Learning Approach to Multi-Omics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Multi-omics approaches have transformed the assessment of biological systems by offering a clear hallmark of intricate diseases. In this work, we introduce a novel ML+DL to improve biomarkers and disease prognosis methods using multi-omics data. Using Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) for feature selection, we combined RF, SVM, and XGB with DNN and LSTM to analyze feature- specific information as well as temporal dependencies in the datasets. Experiments showed that proposed models of SVM+LSTM have the highest accuracy of 98.8%, with SVM+DNN having a slightly lower value of 98.7%. In contrast, RF+DNN and RF+LSTM had acc of 97.5% and 97.1%, respectively, and SVM-based models have an average accuracy of 97.0 to 97.1. Based on these results, the robustness of the hybrid models in capturing intricate relationships across multi- omics layers is demonstrated. Altogether, the outcomes evidentially demonstrate the applicability of novel ML/DL models specifically for individual diagnosis, furthering the therapeutic approach and improving biotechnological processes in both diagnostics and therapeutic applications. Although data integration remains an issue and there are scalability barriers to computation, this work presents a method by which precision medicine can be achieved by linking molecular information to clinics.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Task Offloading and Scheduling in Ultra-Dense MEC for 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)

authors.preferredName: V T Ram Pavan Kumar M

abstract: The paper aims to enhance dynamic request scheduling in ultra-dense networks for 5G systems through MEC. Rising IoT computation demands and enormous data flows have given rise to the need for ultra-dense edge computing (UDEC). Task offloading has been determined as a primary tool in minimizing latency and carrying out flexible computation for the mobile clients. However, there is a significant challenge in catering to the demands of mobile users, as the resources available at the edge fogs are limited, and the user needs are varying. The present study discusses power allocation to mobile clients, and a JRORS scheme, which addresses jointly request offloading and resource scheduling, is designed to reduce energy consumption and latency. The NCGG model addresses the power allocation problem, whereas the MINLP model is built to address the challenge of the JRORS scheme. A MO-NSGA-II algorithm that minimizes response latency and energy consumption is proposed for optimization, while the performance of the scheme is evaluated through simulations in dynamic network scenarios.

Author Keywords: Joint Request Offloading and Resource Scheduling (JRORS)

articleTitle: Diabetic Retinopathy Image Classification using Quasi Cross UNet Discrete Transform with Gold Rush Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy faces three main challenges which include inconsistent image clarity and weak detection of small visual impairments and little ability to share information between different sets of data. The model suffers from two issues which limit its practical use: high expenses for operations as well as low decision accuracy because of complex tissue dynamics. Using the MESSIDOR dataset as input, this paper illustrates the application of the Quasi Cross UNet Discrete Transform with Gold Rush Optimizer (QCUNet-DT-GRO) algorithm for diabetic retinopathy picture categorization. The Unet Swin Transformer (UST) approach is used to precisely segment areas afflicted by diabetic retinopathy, while the Quasi-Cross Bilateral Filtering (QCBF) methodology improves image quality. The One-Dimensional Discrete Transform (ODDT) is used to extract features. The Gold Rush Optimizer (GdRO) does optimization, while the Gates-Controlled Deep Unfolding Network (GCDUNet) handles classification. The system detects diabetic retinopathy along with distinguishing between normal and diabetic retina structures. According to experimental results, QCUNet-DT-GRO performs better than current techniques, with 99.9% accuracy and 99.8% sensitivity. This method is shown to be a viable substitute for the manual diagnostic processes that are now in use, enabling robotic diagnosis systems in subsequent applications.

articleTitle: Stock Market Analysis and Forecasting Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Stock market forecasting and analysis through Deep Learning (DL) methods is the objective of this study, which aims to address the complexity of financial data through the use of advanced predictive modeling. The current research explores Deep Learning (DL) methods used in the stock market analysis and forecasting, tackling financial data complexities through innovative predictive modeling. The intrinsic volatility of stock prices based on numerous economic variables poses an important challenge for which conventional methods of analysis typically fail to achieve a breakthrough. To address the same, an FFNN model was created using historical stock price data to predict future price movement with greater precision. For stock prediction accuracy to be enhanced, a Feedforward Neural Network (FFNN) has been trained using historical stock price data. An FFNN with ReLU activation and Adam optimizer was built and trained following the methodology that comprised data preprocessing, feature selection, normalization, and time-series sequence generation. With a Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss and 80/20 train-test split, the model was trained for more than 50 epochs. Predicted and actual stock prices showed high correlation with slight variations at the peak values. The findings indicate that DL has a great potential for financial prediction and can offer analysts and investors a robust tool. Incorporating sophisticated architectures such as LSTM or GRU, sentiment analysis, and macroeconomic variables might be included in future enhancements to make the predictions even more accurate and versatile.

articleTitle: MediGuide AI using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Providing diverse patient groups with their specific medication requirements, using a wide range of drugs, poses meaningful challenges for prescribing. Standardized approaches often lead to large waste, many side effects and suboptimal outcomes. Therefore, we need improved, more personalized healthcare. MediGuide AI's drug recommendation system is powered by machine learning and it offers a thorough solution. Optimized data pre-processing and analysis, leading to the desired outcome, is achieved using advanced machine learning algorithms like Naive Bayes, TF-IDF and the Natural Language Toolkit. Highly personalized prescriptions are generated using thorough patient data, including demographics and meaningful clinical factors to achieve substantially better accuracy. Important enhancements include dual recommendation outputs, which provide many drug recommendations alongside a large number of alternative Ayurvedic treatments presented side by side for effortless comparison. An advanced personalized dosage calculation module precisely determines drug dosages using advanced regression models based on age, weight and metabolism. This system helps patients track and record their medications and it also suggests several nearby Ayurvedic shops based on their location. MediGuide AI employs exceptionally powerful algorithms and its advanced tools deliver remarkably precise and exceptionally user-friendly healthcare solutions. Current systems make use of rule-based methods that cannot learn from new data, whereas MediGuide AI leverages a hybrid Naïve Bayes and PassiveAggressiveClassifier model for higher accuracy and real-time adaptability. It also includes Ayurvedic options to ensure personalized healthcare experience.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning for Personalized Cardiovascular Risk Prediction from Multi-Lead ECG Signal
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Despite multiple efforts, cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) still top the list of leading causes of mortality worldwide and require early and personalised risk prediction strategies. Current ECG based risk assessment models are limited to generalizing to varying patient populations and suffer poor interpatient variability. The contribution of this paper is a personalized cardiovascular risk prediction from multi lead ECG signals using a contrastive learning framework. The model learns robust patient specific representations via a self-supervised learning technique that does not require large amounts of labeled data. The deep neural network trained with the contrastive loss function effectively discriminates high and low risk ECG patterns by maximizing the similarity of positive pairs (ECG signals from the same patient or similar risk profile) and minimizing negative pair similarity. Evaluation of the proposed approach is carried out on publicly available ECG datasets resulting in better predictive performance than traditional supervised learning methods. Improved generalization obtained with this framework makes it a promising early diagnosis and personalized cardiovascular health monitoring tool.

articleTitle: Semantic-and Relation-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Secure Routing in VANETs to Avoid Blackhole Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Vehicular Ad-hoc NETworking (VANET) is one of the latest generations of wireless networks which enable the application of combined and smooth data transmission between automobiles but it encounters varieties of problems one of which is black hole attack in which the malicious nodes alter the packets thus causing the interruption of communication. In light of these problems, this paper proposes the Osprey Semantic-and Relation-aware Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with Snow Geese Algorithm (OSRHGNNet-SGA). To enhance networking organization, this technique starts followed by the construction of construction clusters using OOA. It then employs a Semantic-and Relation-aware Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (SR-HGNN) to accurately locate black hole attacks. Finally, the presented Snow Geese Algorithm SGA improves the channels for data transmission to ensure safe routing. The suggested method has 99.64 % correct identification ratio, 3000 bytes/sec throughput, latencies below 3 seconds and a PDR of the 98 % meaning it is reliable and efficient solution for safe communication in VANETs.

Author Keywords: Semantic-and Relation-aware Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network

articleTitle: High-Performance Secure File Sharing with Dual Server Access and Time-Sensitive Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Cloud computing is emerging as a predominant interactive framework for accessing users' data stored remotely on an Internet cloud server. Cloud services provide substantial benefits, allowing the customers to utilize on-demand apps irrespective of their local infrastructure limitations. During data access, several users are collaborated. It makes data sharing essential for realizing productive advantages. This project provides a collaborative governance paradigm for data sharing to address the previously noted privacy issues in cloud storage. The project achieves shared access authority via a method for matching anonymous access requests, addressing security and privacy concerns. Data access is granted only with the approval from cloud infrastructure and file owner. The shared access authority obtains and distributes the data solicited by users. This project enhancement entails a time-server access mechanism for secure data retrieval in the cloud, with files encrypted before storage. The encryption process utilizes symmetric key cryptography. The user secures authorization from a primary server to access the file directory or locate a specific file. The primary server recognizes the user's request and permits to select a file from the list. Then, the file owner receives an access request and upon acceptance, grants the secret key to the requesting user. It allows in viewing and downloading the material. If the user fails to submit a request within seconds, the primary server redirect to the mainpage. If the users need access to the file list again, the users have to obtain authorization from the primary server.

articleTitle: Literature Review on Optimizing Cash Flow Forecasting Using Machine Learning in Small and Medium Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research aims to assess how the application of machine learning (ML) can enhance the accuracy and efficiency of cash flow forecasting in small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and to identify the relationship between ML adoption and improved financial decision-making within these enterprises. The methodology used is a systematic literature review following the PRISMA framework. The analysis is based on selected papers that meet specific criteria and address the research questions of this study. The findings reveal that various ML models can enhance cash flow forecasting by utilizing financial data and capturing underlying patterns. The study concludes that ML is beneficial for SMEs, helping to reduce insolvency rates through improved cash flow forecasting and enabling better financial decision-making based on wellmanaged financial data.

articleTitle: Enhancing Intrusion Detection Systems Using RNN, LSTM, and Hybrid RNN-LSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Due to The lack of comparison studies and practical applications of RNN, LSTM, and hybrid RNN-LSTM models for intrusion detection systems, especially when managing class imbalances in complex network datasets, represents a gap in the literature. This study investigates the application of deep learning techniques to improve the detection capabilities of IDS. For this study, we applied and assessed Recurrent Neural Network, Long Short-Term Memory, and Hybrid RNN-LSTM models on a UNSW-NB15 dataset, and to redress class imbalance we trained and validated our models using synthetic minority over-sampling. The RNN-LSTM model was shown to perform the best with a 9 4. 0 0 % accuracy in comparison to other models. These experimental results signify the possibility of enhancing IDS performance and a dependable method of detecting various network intrusions with the use of hybrid models comprised of RNN & LSTM.

articleTitle: Efficient LLMs for Edge Devices: Pruning, Quantization, and Distillation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Due to their size and processing demands, Large Language Models (LLMs) are challenging to implement on edge devices with constrained resources, such as mobile phones and Internet of Things platforms. To address these restrictions, this work investigates optimization methodologies, including knowledge distillation, Quantization, and model pruning. Model pruning diminished the model's size by as much as 60%, reducing it from 500 MB to 200 MB while maintaining an accuracy of 89.5% and decreasing inference time to 125 ms. Quantization achieved a 91.2% accuracy while reducing the memory footprint by 50%, decreasing memory usage from 500 MB to 250 MB. The inference time was enhanced from 150 ms to 110 ms. By reducing the model size to 250 MB and halving the training duration from 30 to 15 hours, knowledge distillation successfully conveyed knowledge from a teacher model to a student model, achieving 85.0% of the teacher model's correctness. The findings indicate that information distillation, Quantization, and pruning collaboratively facilitate the effective deployment of LLMs on edge devices, unlocking their potential for real-time applications in resource-limited environments.

articleTitle: Localization in 6G Communication Networks Using Low Complex Time of Arrival (TOA) and Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Optimal placement of sensor nodes is a challenging issue in localization applications because the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) of target nodes dependent on the sensor node geometry. Though there exists many localization algorithms and methods, localization using time of arrival (TOA) and time difference of arrival (TDOA) of wideband signals has potential features to support higher accuracy at lower complexity, these techniques become a promising choice for various applications including underwater communication, highly precise radar systems, and radio communication. However, multipath propagation (the combination of indirect path signals between target node and anchor nodes), lack of clock synchronization, computational complexity, high power consumption, interference, and noise pose major challenges that affect the localization accuracy. In this paper, a highly accurate and simplified versions of TOA, TDOA-based localization techniques are presented that suit the resource constraint applications of industrial internet of things (IIoT) and 6G communication systems. The proposed TOA, TDOA techniques are based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) channel estimation that ensures reliable location estimations and is less susceptible to multipath effects. During TOA based location measurements, perfect synchronization is ensured between anchor nodes and target nodes. In case of TDOA based location measurements, though the target node is not synchronized with the anchor nodes still all the anchor nodes are synchronized. So, the synchronization error between the target node and all anchor nodes is the same. Therefore, the proposed TDOA measurements and the localization accuracy are independent of synchronization error. Simulations were conducted using fast Fourier transform (FFT) and MUSIC spectrum analysis methods at higher frequency bands under noisy environments and results are compared with the performance under ideal conditions. The results proved that both TOA and TDOA based localization values are very close to the corresponding ideal value conditions and immune to noisy environments. Overall, TDOA based localization outperforms TOA based localization technique.

articleTitle: Predicting Quality Emotions for Human-Like Behavior in AI-Generated Text through NLP Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This work enhances sentiment analysis and emotion classification in low-resource languages by addressing cultural nuances, dataset biases, and evaluation inconsistencies. The proposed framework comprises three key components. First, it distinguishes between AI-generated and human-generated text to ensure that emotions are extracted only from genuine human expressions, maintaining the authenticity of emotion analysis. Second, it employs NLP techniques to accurately detect and classify emotions such as joy, sadness, anger, and fear, ensuring a deeper understanding of human sentiment. Finally, it simulates human-like responses by mapping detected emotions to probable human behaviors, enhancing AI's emotional intelligence and relatability. By reducing reliance on Large Language Models (LLMs), this approach improves accuracy, fairness, and efficiency, resulting in more inclusive and reliable sentiment analysis systems across diverse linguistic and cultural contexts.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Smart Health Care Predictions Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Smart Health Prediction Using Machine Learning” is a state-of-the-art, advanced system that will use high-power predictive modeling to predict diseases based on the entered symptoms. The proposed system will go through a multistage process to maintain accuracy in the predictions. First, it pre-processes the data by handling missing values and scaling features. It selects the relevant features based on symptoms from the dataset to enhance the accuracy of the prediction. The data is divided according to training and testing. The algorithm used here is SVM, since it can easily handle high complexity in data and feature space and capture the nonlinear relationships. The training of the SVM model consists of setting a suitable value for the hyperparameters such as kernel type and regularization. The model evaluation is done based on accuracy metrics and classification reports. After the training and validation, the model is deployed in real time for healthcare scenarios. Continuous monitoring and maintenance will be done to ensure accuracy and relevance of the model with respect to disease prediction. The SVM algorithm stands proud at an impressive rate of 90% as compared to other algorithms such as Random Forest, Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Decision Trees. Therefore, being able to handle such complex and high-dimensional health-care prediction datasets while capturing the nonlinear data relationships with great efficiency makes the model a major choice for real-time disease forecasting.

articleTitle: Real-Time GPS Tracking and Health Monitoring for Animals Using IoT and Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) grounded solution of Real Time Global Positioning System (GPS) tracking with Health Monitoring of Animals for Owners to track their animals like cows, buffaloes, dogs etc. This GPS module and a heartbeat sensor are attached to the animals in order to be able to follow them closely. This data is sent to a mobile app, and the owner can see their heart on the map as well as monitor its pulse. Based on analysis of such heart rate variations, the system determines when it is seeing an abnormal activity related to e.g. stress (increased heart rate) or potential health risks (no sign of a heartbeat), which could be interpreted as fear or death. Each animal has an initial heart rate level that is set, and when this rate exceeds it, the system sounds an alert to indicate danger. This method is especially helpful for keeping an eye on animals in urban areas, areas close to forests, and areas with high rates of theft and loss. The project demonstrates the successful execution of a reliable, real-time animal monitoring system with practical applications in both urban and rural environments.

articleTitle: Skin Lesion Classification Using Feature Extraction and Ensemble Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This study explores a feature-engineering approach for classifying skin lesions as benign or malignant. Many other approaches regarding feature extraction can be applied: color, texture, shape, Gabor filters, Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), edge density, fractal dimension, wavelet analysis, and entropy. It then gives a computationally efficient alternative instead of deep learning models. A soft-voting approach based on an ensemble of machine learning classifiers: SVM, MLP, and Random Forest is proposed. articleTitle: Traffic Surveillance System Through Capsule Gated Graph Attention Network for IoT/IIoT Cyberthreat Detection and Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Internet of Things and Industrial Internet of Things have seen rapid adoption and have transformed industries through smart automation, constant monitoring and better connected systems. The progressive inclusion of such solutions has contributed to the growth in exposure to complex and changing global threats. The primary challenge lies in accurately detecting and classifying cyber threats from high-volume, unstructured network traffic data in real-time. Existing methods are not very accurate and cannot be easily scaled due to constraints in computational resources and the nature of IIoT network systems. This paper introduces Traffic Surveillance System through Capsule Gated Graph Attention Network for IoT/IIoT Cyberthreat Detection and Mitigation (Cyber-CapG). The system uses raw traffic data from Edge-IIoTset and uses the Tunable Transformer for feature extraction. The extracted features are passed through the Capsule Gated Graph Attention Network to model the traffic as a graph based on communication hierarchy and being selective to essential traffic patterns. Furthermore, weights and loss functions are tuned based on the Progressive Crested Porcupine Optimization so as to achieve maximum optimization. The proposed system exhibits outstanding performance with 99.21 % detection rate, 99.07% precision, 99.15% recall, 99.18% F1 measure, and it provides an effective way of identifying threats like DDoS, SQL Injection, and Ransomware. In conclusion, Cyber-CapG provides a solid solution for traffic surveillance in IoT/IIoT, providing the high detection and prevention of various cyber threats, as well as optimizing the cybersecurity and reliability of industrial networks.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Management with AI Driven Analytics in Solar Energy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven framework for real-time smart grid optimization tailored specifically for solar energy integration. The proposed system features a multi-layered architecture that integrates data acquisition from solar irradiance sensors, smart meters, and meteorological sources with advanced pre-processing techniques to ensure data quality and fusion. Using advanced deep learning architectures, such as Long Short-Term Memory networks for forecasting solar irradiance and regression methodologies for predicting load, our proposed framework dynamically adjusts energy dispatch and demand response measures to address the inherent variability associated with solar power. Additionally, a combined strategy that incorporates reinforcement learning is implemented to improve real-time grid stability and operational efficiency, and explainable artificial intelligence methods are used to provide clarity in decision-making processes. Simulation studies conducted on an enhanced IEEE 24-bus test system have shown to reduce forecast error by up to 30% and prevent the occurrence of grid instability events by about 40% in contrast with traditional methods. These results are promising for AI-based analytics since it promises to enhance smart grid functionality and enable more sustainable use of renewable resources. Further research will develop this model with additional renewable energy sources and increase cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Stereoscopic Gated Graph Scalable Quantum Capsule Convolutional Neural Networks with Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm for Social Media Content Classification and Community Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Social Media Content Classification and Community Detection (SMCCCD) classify content and identify communities through deep learning, and NLP. Traditional models are weak in scalability and interpretability. To solve all these problems, this paper introduces a Stereoscopic Gated Graph Scalable Quantum Capsule Convolutional Neural Networks with Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (SGGSQCCN2Nets+AHA) for social content classification and community detection. Data inputs are accessed from the Twitter dataset and are initially preprocessed by the Natural Language (NL) method. After preprocessing, content classification and community detection are done using the Stereoscopic Gated Graph Scalable Quantum Capsule Convolutional Neural Networks (SGGSQCCN2Nets) and optimization is then performed with the Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA). The performance of the new SGGSQCCN2Nets+AHA model is tested on a Twitter dataset with a high accuracy rate of 99.9% and specificity of 99.8%. The proposed model is developed by utilizing Python programming language. The outcome of the proposed SGGSQCCN2Nets+AHA model enhances the performance of content classification and improves user community detection accuracy. It is effective in addressing scalability issues, obtaining complex features, and offering more interpretability. The model is also resilient against noisy data dynamically adapts to evolving social media trends and outperforms traditional deep learning techniques in real-time analysis.

Author Keywords: Social Media Content Classification and Community Detection
