articleTitle: Risk-Adapted Breast Cancer Screening: Combining DOT and Ultrasound with AI to Overcome Mammography Limitations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: For more than four decades, clinicians have used mammography, the gold standard imaging technique, to screen populations for breast cancer. Nevertheless, the uncritical character of population-based screening is challenged by mammography's sensitivity limitations and high false-positive rates, especially in high-risk women. There may be new possibilities for screening approaches thanks to recent developments in breast imaging technology, such as contrast material enhanced mammography (CEM), ultrasound (US) (automated-breast US, Doppler, elastography US), besides MRI in particular. Additionally, risk-adapted screening could be improved through the combination of AI and radiomics methods. One exciting new tool for studying tumor angiogenesis is diffuse optical tomography, or DOT. Reconstructing a breast lesion's DOT function map, however, is an illposed and undecided inverse operation. To enhance the localization and precision of DOT reconstruction, a co-registered ultrasonography (US) technology that offers structural information about the breast lesion can be utilized. Further improvement in cancer detection based on DOT alone is possible with the well-known US features of benign and malignant breast lesions. to build a new neural network for diagnosis by combining US features extracted from six different neural networks (Xception, InceptionV3, VGG16, MobileNet, and ResNet50) with images reconstructed from a DOT deep learning auto-encoder-based model. This approach was inspired by a fusion model deep learning strategy. The F1-score, recall, precision, and accuracy were the metrics utilized to assess each model. Collection of records Improved accuracy in both the suggested model and the fine-tuned pretrained models was a result of the beneficial effects of boosting, preprocessing, and balancing on breast cancer detection and classification.

articleTitle: Next Word Prediction Using Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Next-word prediction is a fundamental task in natural language processing (NLP) with various applications in intelligent text completion, voice assistants, and human-computer interaction. Most statistical model-based or deep learning-based methods tend to have difficulty modeling both semantic knowledge and long-range contextual dependencies. This work introduces a hybrid next-word prediction model that combines Knowledge Graph (KG) embeddings and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to improve semantic consciousness and sequential context representation. By tapping into structured relational knowledge in KGs together with the contextual learning abilities of LSTMs, the approach here seeks to enhance predictive precision and semantic consistency. This research fills the gap between structured knowledge representation and neural sequence modeling, paving the way for more context-sensitive and semantically richer next-word prediction models.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Health Care Computing and Assessments in Oman: an Effectual Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Health care plays a vital responsibility in a human life span. World countries targets to provide better care for their citizens. Digital transformations and innovations in Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies helps in deep for the novel solutions to speed-up the decision making process in health management and patient consulting. AI branches including Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Neural Networks (NN), Natural Language Processing (NLP) and so forth can support innovations in heal care domain. This paper presents the comprehensive and noble review on recent existing tools and techniques and also recommends advanced techniques for health care industry that are to be used in Sultanate of Oman. Furthermore, overcoming AI challenges are resulted and presented through the study. This work mainly aimed to produce the multiple dimensions and challenges that helps to develop AI powered real-life applications in health care support system.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Pedagogical Word Recommendation Systems Transforming English as a Second Language Vocabulary Learning Effectiveness

articleTitle: ResNet-GRU Hybrid Model for Brain Tumor Diagnosis: A Sequential Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research investigates the effectiveness of integrating Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), a variant of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), into pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) such as Residual Networks (ResNet50) for enhanced brain tumor classification using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans. RNNs are a class of Neural Networks (NNs) structured to analyze sequential data, while GRU is a specific type of RNN that efficiently learns long-term dependencies without suffering from vanishing gradients. ResNet50 is a robust architecture renowned for its exceptional image feature extraction capabilities. GRU specializes in modeling complex temporal relationships. By integrating these two, this approach effectively synergizes the strengths of both architectures to achieve enhanced performance. This combination enables the model to capture spatial and temporal dependencies in MRI scans, improving brain tumor classification accuracy. Using the publicly available “Br35H: Brain Tumor Detection 2020” dataset, we evaluate the effectiveness of the suggested ResNet50-GRU model, achieving state-of-the-art results. This comprehensive evaluation employs various metrics, such as Accuracy, Cohen's Kappa, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), Area Under the Curve (AUC), Precision, Recall, and F1-score. The results underscore the advantages of combining CNNs and GRUs for medical image analysis. This study provides valuable insights for developing more accurate and efficient Deep Learning (DL) based diagnostic tools, highlighting the prospects of CNN-RNN combinations in medical imaging applications.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Resource Allocation in C-V2X Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Ensuring smooth data interchange between vehicles and infrastructure depends on the smart use of communication resources, including bandwidth, power, and time slots. The framework must respond to user specific requirements, adjust to changing network conditions, and maximize efficiency while minimizing interference. Nevertheless, it has several challenges, such as limited resources, excessive energy consumption, and delays caused due to frequent topological changes by vehicle mobility. This paper proposes the Hierarchical Meta Reinforcement Learning framework based on Information Volume Evidential Markov Decision Processes to address these challenges. Unlike conventional reinforcement learning techniques, this methodology uses hierarchical reinforcement learning to make adaptive decisions in challenging situations. Additionally, by utilizing previously learned policies, it uses meta-learning to facilitate quick tasks adaption, increasing operational efficiency and flexibility. The proposed method achieves a highest V2V link success probability of 98% for 100 vehicles outperforming other techniques like MA-DDQN.

Author Keywords: Information volume evidential Markov decision process

articleTitle: An Advanced Imaging and Machine Learning Algorithm for Enhanced Oral Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Oral cancer is a major public health problem threatening populations throughout the world, and early detection plays an essential role in enhancing both patient survival rates corresponding associated long-term outcomes of treatment. Significant advancements in imaging technology and machine learning algorithms have heralded new avenues to better diagnostic accuracy. This paper contains an exhaustive evaluation of the AIOCD performance against its two well established models, namely HNB-PDP A Model and EIDR model. The evaluation was performed at different number of image sets namely 100,200,300,400 and 500 along with key performance metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 Score, AUC and Training Time. The results of our experiments demonstrate that the AIOCD algorithm is uniformly more accurate than qualitatively similar models while achieving competitive accuracy, precision, recall and area under ROC with their trade-offs in learning times. The current results highlighted the capacity of AIOCD algorithm to serve as a promising and useful tool for reliable, rapid oral cancer detection that would help further improve early or accurate diagnosis in clinical practices.

articleTitle: Development of Machine Leaning Based Safety Helmet Detection using Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: A Strict safety regulations exist in hazardous industries, such as construction and mining. However, there is continued non-compliance with helmet-wearing policies and continued risks due to this action. Traditional methods of manual monitoring are inefficient and prone to error. Existing automated detection systems often struggle with challenges such as occlusion, low-light environments, and complex backgrounds, resulting in unreliable performance. Due to complex and diverse environment most, existing system have difficulty in detecting overlapping and small object. This paper introduces a real-time Safety Helmet Detection system by utilizing the YOLOv8 model in addressing these problems. The detection accuracy is also improved in situations of occlusion, low light conditions, and cluttered backgrounds. Also, the system is optimized for edge devices with minimal computational overhead. Compliance checks in automation through video feeds from surveillance cameras minimize the risk of head injuries, thus ensuring a safer work environment. Its integration into workplace management software ensures real-time reporting, thus minimizing manual intervention for better effectiveness in enforcement

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Model for Anomaly Detection in Data Streaming - Data Engineering Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to implement a transfer learning model for predicting anomalies in online streaming data. Streaming data is a continuous data generation and transmission model with a huge amount of data, enabling different kinds of vulnerable attacks in the network. It leads to negative impacts on the overall network performance. Several earlier methods have been proposed to improve anomaly detection accuracy in streaming data, whereas the false positive rate is high. This paper has aimed to increase the anomaly detection rate with a reduced false positive rate. Hence, it proposed a novel transfer learning method for designing an effective anomaly detection model in data streaming applications. It implements a long., short-term memory for managing the continuous generation and transfer of data called streaming data because it has multiple built-in features like forget gate., which operates the memory by eliminating unwanted and redundant data flows in the streaming process. The LSTM model is deployed in a kind of MANET called VANET, where it is applied to detect anomalies during vehicle communication. This paper provides high prediction accuracy since it integrates various data analytics tasks, like preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification, which feed quality data and perform fast analysis. The LSTM can detect anomalies, including DoS, DDoS, Sybil, Sinkhole, Wormhole, and blackhole. The simulation is carried out by implementing LSTM in Python and executed on a benchmark dataset to verify the efficacy of LSTM. The output shows that the model provides higher accuracy, low latency, and high throughput and is suitable for many real-time applications like IoT networks and cybersecurity.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Learning-Based Q-Commerce Framework Evolving from E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The rapid evolution of E-Commerce has led to the emergence of Quick Commerce (Q-Commerce), a model that prioritizes ultra-fast deliveries and real-time decision-making. This paper proposes a Hybrid Learning-based framework that enhances Q-Commerce operations by integrating Self-Supervised, Supervised, Reinforcement, and Unsupervised Learning techniques. The model leverages BERT for self-supervised pretraining, enabling context-aware customer personalization and improved search relevance. LSTMs and CNNs are employed for demand forecasting and product classification, ensuring optimized inventory management. GNNs enhance personalized recommendations by analyzing user-product relationships. For logistics optimization, DQN and PPO are implemented to dynamically adjust last-mile delivery routes, reducing delivery times and operational costs. To ensure fraud prevention, AEs and GANs detect anomalous transaction behaviors, improving security while minimizing false positives. The proposed hybrid deployment strategy, combining cloud-based AI inference and Edge AI at micro-fulfillment centers (MFCs), enhances system responsiveness and scalability. The framework is evaluated using MAE, RMSE, HR, Fl-Score, and ROC curves, ensuring accurate demand prediction, optimized logistics, and effective fraud detection. Future advancements in Autonomous Deliveries, AI-Powered Warehousing, and Blockchain Integration will further revolutionize Q-Commerce, making it an indispensable extension of E-Commerce.

articleTitle: GuavaCareNet: Empowering Guava Farms with Federated Learning for Real-Time Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research presents a Federated Learning-based approach for the detection of guava leaf diseases, aimed at enhancing agricultural practices while ensuring data privacy. Guava farms across various regions provide images of guava leaves, both healthy and diseased, to train a deep learning model for disease classification. The EfficientNet-B3 model, optimized with Neural Architecture Search (NAS) and Transfer Learning, is used for accurate disease detection, including conditions like Anthracnose and Powdery Mildew. To ensure privacy, Federated Learning (FL) is employed, where the model is trained locally on edge devices such as smartphones and Jetson Nano devices situated at guava farms. These devices process the data locally and send model updates, rather than raw data, to a central server. This method enables the aggregation of knowledge from multiple farms without sharing sensitive information, thereby protecting farmers' data privacy. The use of Federated Learning allows the model to adapt to specific conditions at each farm, such as different diseases, leaf appearances, and lighting variations, improving its robustness and accuracy. Additionally, AWS IoT integration allows real-time monitoring and alerts, further empowering farmers with timely disease detection. The decentralized nature of this approach not only enhances disease detection in guava crops but also fosters data privacy, ensuring farmers' information remains secure.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Accessibility: Smart Reader as an Assistive Tool for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The amalgamation of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) has greatly improved accessibility for visually impaired individuals, fostering increased autonomy through pioneering assistive technology. This study introduces the Smart Reader, a device that integrates optical character recognition (OCR) and text-to-speech (TTS) technologies to enhance accessibility to printed documents. The Smart Reader utilizes a camera to take text images, translates them into digital representation through OCR, and converts the text into audible speech via TTS. The system has an intuitive user interface, an automatic page-turning mechanism, and a dictionary lookup function, guaranteeing a seamless reading experience. The findings indicate that the Smart Reader significantly improves access to written information, hence enhancing the quality of life for visually impaired individuals, especially in educational environments such as schools and libraries. The device is engineered for user-friendliness, enhancing accessibility and autonomy. The Smart Reader utilizes AI and ML, marking a significant progression in assistive technology, promoting an inclusive society where visually impaired individuals can engage with printed material with assurance. In addition to functionality, it seeks to empower people by connecting capability with opportunity, guaranteeing equitable access to information for everyone.

articleTitle: Crack Detection and Structural Assessment in Bridges Using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Crack detection is essential for maintaining the safety and durability of infrastructure like bridges and buildings. Traditional methods, relying on manual inspections and basic photographic analysis, are inefficient and prone to error, with limited annotated datasets posing a major challenge for automation. This paper proposes a novel framework using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to generate realistic, high-resolution synthetic crack images with pixel-level annotations. By leveraging Deep Convolutional GANs (DCGANs), the framework addresses dataset scarcity, enabling deep neural networks (DNNs) to achieve higher accuracy in crack detection tasks. The generated synthetic datasets enhance model performance, reduce reliance on manual data annotation, and support scalable training. Additionally, GANs facilitate transfer learning, allowing DNNs trained on synthetic data to adapt effectively to real-world scenarios. Beyond crack detection, this method shows potential for broader structural health monitoring, including detecting corrosion, surface degradation, and material defects, making it a versatile solution for infrastructure safety and integrity.

articleTitle: Enhancing Edge Performance: A Comparative Analysis of LSTM Inference Using Hardware Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) provide compelling advantages for accelerating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, particularly in edge computing applications where performance and power efficiency are critical. This study presents an optimized FPGA-based LSTM accelerator implemented using High-Level Synthesis (HLS) on the PYNQ Z2 board. The proposed design achieves 3.71x performance improvement over a software-based implementation running on the Processing System (PS) of the PYNQ Z2, reducing execution time significantly. The accelerator efficiently utilizes FPGA resources, with 63% LUT and 61% DSP utilization, ensuring a balanced trade-off between computational throughput and hardware constraints. Power analysis reveals that hardware consumes very small fraction of the total power. This study demonstrates that FPGA-based LSTM accelerators provide significant speedup and energy efficiency, making them an attractive solution for real-time, resource-constrained machine learning applications at edge.

articleTitle: An Enhanced MPPT Control for PV with Grid Connected EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research introduces a new approach to optimizing energy harvest from photovoltaic (PV) systemsan enhanced Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control strategy that makes use of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). Due to falling EV demand, grid- connected EV charging facilities that include solar PV systems are gaining prominence as a renewable energy source. Conventional MPPT techniques, such as incremental conductance and perturb and observe, often underperform when confronted with dynamic environmental conditions. To circumvent these restrictions, this study employs ANN's adaptive learning capabilities to forecast, given changing factors such as solar irradiance, temperature, as well as load conditions, the PV system's best operating points. A complete PV array, an interconnection to the grid, and a highly efficient electric vehicle charging station are all components of the suggested system design. The efficient and dependable charging of electric vehicles is guaranteed by the ANN- based MPPT controller, which is designed to increase the energy production from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P V$</tex> array. The experimental findings show that when it comes to energy harvesting efficiency, the ANN-based MPPT is much better than the older approaches, especially when the sun's intensity is changing. This research demonstrates how control algorithms powered by ANNs may revolutionize the integration of solar energy with electric car infrastructure. The broad use of renewable energy sources is also encouraged by this initiative, which helps to improve grid stability. To further enhance system efficiency and scalability, future research will investigate the integration of additional renewable sources with hybrid MPPT approaches. This will help to create an energy ecosystem that is more sustainable.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Tomato Leaf Disease Detection: A Counting Sort-Enhanced Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Tomato leaf diseases cause large output losses and are a serious threat to agricultural productivity. Timely intervention and efficient illness treatment depend on early and precise disease identification. This study enhances a Counting Sort-based feature engineering strategy to offer a unique deep learning approach for tomato leaf disease diagnosis. Conventional image-based techniques for illness identification frequently suffer from feature redundancy and computational complexity. To overcome these obstacles, we preprocess and extract pertinent characteristics from tomato leaf photos by utilizing Counting Sort's efficiency. In particular, the distribution of pixel intensities within particular color channels is analyzed using Counting Sort, which makes it possible to identify important textural and color-based characteristics linked to various illness kinds. These characteristics are then used to train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture, which is used to categorize tomato leaves into early blight, late blight, and healthy disease categories. A dataset of tomato leaf photos that are openly accessible is used to assess the effectiveness of the suggested method. According to experimental results, the Counting Sort-enhanced deep learning model outperforms conventional deep learning approaches that depend on generic feature extraction techniques or raw pixel data in terms of accuracy and processing speed. This method provides a viable way to identify tomato leaf disease automatically and effectively, which will enhance farming methods and increase food security.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of Transfer Learning Models for Deep Fake Image Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Deepfake identifies fake videos and photographs. To create deepfakes, machine learning algorithms change video or reputation features like faces. Deepfake identifies fake videos and photographs. New deep learning generative algorithms may make fake films and photos seem real, worrying many. Personal and social safety are jeopardized. We urgently need computational methods to detect fake material and alert consumers of picture and video changes. We evaluate deep learning-based deepfake detection. We want to automate field development fake content detection. Assessing the work's strengths and faults, we find deepfakes. AI, NLP, and computer vision use deep machine learning for efficiency and usability. Deepfakes create realistic images and videos using deep learning. We test multiple deep learning-based deepfake detection and generation approaches. Several deepfake detection techniques are examined. Researchers benefit from our paper's social media deepfake detection. Compare current and previous industrial practices and datasets.

articleTitle: Validation of Generative Visual Solutions Using Prompt Engineering and Caption Based Visual Reasoning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: We introduce the novel approach of validation of artificially generated images which helps to validate the images based on the prompt given for the generated image. Existing methods involve generation of images based on the prompts, diffusion of images and modification of images, but fail to determine the correctness of the generated image with respect to the generated content and prompt given at user end. The prompt used for generating the image using generative artificial intelligence solutions can be comprehensive and can hold more than single perspective. To address this issue while validating computer visual solutions, we propose a method for the validation of generative visual solutions using prompt engineering and caption based visual reasoning models. The proposed solution determines the different perspectives and comprehensiveness of the prompts based on entities and attributes and then, multiple test cases are formed considering different perspectives, in more detailed and comprehensive format. Hence, proposed solution validates the generated image based on the text prompt engineered for comprehensive understanding based on the complexity of the prompt suitable for visual reasoning models.

articleTitle: Drug Recommendation System Using Patient Reviews Based on Sentimental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The integration of digital technology in healthcare has been greatly facilitated by the internet. It has made access to vital data quite easy, with which solutions created help in improving patient outcomes. This leads to an improvement in patient care and medical procedures. Vigilance is required to avoid the dissemination of information that may be incorrect or dangerous, and thus harm patients and healthcare providers alike. The amount of patient-generated data involved is huge, and this has become quite central to the drug recommendation system in the healthcare industry. It is envisioned that medication recommendations by these systems are highly precise to increase efficacy and accuracy of treatment. Using Natural Language Processing tools, the suggested approach will make a prediction about the best drug, using ratings and reviews made by the patients. It would be advisable to apply some NLP approaches to the input provided by the patient to extract some useful insights and information that might help in prescription decisions. Examples of some machine learning methods applied for enhancing accuracy and dependability of such drug recommendations include the XGBoost classifier and LightGBM model. These algorithms further process and analyse data to bring out the relationships and patterns not otherwise evident. They therefore provide crucial help toward the formation and establishment of an effective or reliable drug-related recommendation system and greatly improved the treatment of patients.

articleTitle: Feature Enriched Speech Emotion Recognition Using Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Accurate Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) continues to be a challenging task due to differences in speech patterns and interference from environmental noise. This paper tackles these challenges by introducing a deep learning-based solution that leverages audio data from the CREMA, RAVDESS, SAVEE, and TESS datasets. To process the data, this research extracts Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) as key features and implement a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to analyze temporal and spectral patterns in the audio. The model incorporates dropout regularization to improve generalization and employs data augmentation techniques to enhance its robustness. Our method achieves consistent emotion classification, making a valuable contribution to the fields of human-computer interaction and affective computing.

articleTitle: Smart Parking Management System for University
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: University campuses face a parking congestion due to limited space availability and inefficient parking management, leading to wasted time, increased fuel consumption, and traffic congestion. This study developed an intelligent parking management system-integrating image processing for automatic license plate recognition and Dijkstra's Algorithm to optimize route selection; ensuring drivers reach available slots with minimal delay. The system features real-time updates, automated slot reservations, and guided navigation, significantly enhancing efficiency. Evaluation based on ISO/IEC 25010 software quality standards yielded high ratings in functionality (3.30), usability (3.33), reliability (3.18), and efficiency (3.24), indicating strong system performance. The study concludes that integrating automated parking solutions with AI-driven optimization can significantly improve parking space utilization and reduce congestion. Future enhancements include expanding database capacity, upgrading image processing accuracy, and integrating IoT sensors for real-time monitoring, ensuring a more scalable and sustainable parking solution.

articleTitle: Advanced Vision-Language Pipelines: Contextual Learning and Interactive Segmentation for Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Medical imaging plays a pivotal role in modern diagnostics, yet existing AI-based pipelines face significant challenges, including reliance on proprietary datasets, limited modality support, and inadequate explainability. This research introduces a scalable, end-to-end pipeline that integrates anomaly detection, segmentation, and diagnostic report generation to address these limitations. By leveraging a VisualLanguage Model (VLM) trained on context-rich image-text pairs generated from open-source label-only datasets using a fine-tuned Large Language Model (LLM), the system ensures scalability across modalities and protects patient privacy by eliminating reliance on proprietary medical data. Interactive, text-driven segmentation is achieved through the integration of a CLIP-based Segment Anything Model (CLIP-SAM), enabling clinicians to refine anomaly boundaries with high precision. A fine-tuned LLaMA-based LLM, employing Chain-of-Thought reasoning, generates detailed, actionable diagnostic reports tailored to clinical needs. Experimental evaluations on MRI, CT, and X-ray datasets demonstrate an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.91 for anomaly detection, a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 84.5 % for segmentation, and a BLEU score of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8 5. 6 \%}$</tex> for report quality, significantly surpassing state-of-the-art baselines. This robust and explainable framework establishes a new standard for automated medical imaging analysis, supporting diverse imaging modalities and aligning AIgenerated insights with clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: A Review on Web Data Mining to Detect Online Spread of Terrorism Activity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research study outlines the significant contribution that web data mining can make in discovering and combating the dissemination of online terrorism. With terrorist groups using the internet more and more to deliver propaganda, recruit, and organize, there is a pressing need for efficient monitoring and analysis of web content. This article discusses different data mining methods that can be used to identify and study patterns suggestive of terrorist activity throughout networked digital environments. Specifically, the embedding of machine learning algorithms, i.e., Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, is investigated with regard to its suitability to differentiate between benign and harmful online content. These algorithms can process large volumes of data, where features are extracted, including URL structures, domain ages, and keyword frequencies, to detect anticipate threats. According to the article, feature extraction plays a crucial role in improving detection system accuracy, enabling real-time surveillance of anomalous online activities. In addition, the review discusses the problems that researchers and law enforcement agencies have been encountering in using web data mining for counter-terrorism purposes. Ethical concerns around privacy and civil liberties are addressed and technical challenges, including the quality of data and the dynamic character of online content, are elaborated. Scenarios in which false positives arising in detection systems may occur are also considered, with emphasis on the need for ongoing algorithm and technique refinement.

Author Keywords: Precision Agriculture Pest and disease management remote sensing and crop protection

articleTitle: Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease Using Machine Learning and Neuroimaging Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is one of the largest challenges faced in modern medicine, and this form of dementia has symptoms ranging from basic cognitive decline to specific neurodegenerative changes due to genetics. Early and correct diagnosis are needed for timely intervention and management of the disease. We propose a cutting-edge study, DeepAD-Net, which involves creating as well as training of deep learning kind algorithm to improve the detection rate in early stages for Alzheimer's disease via combination of all data from clinical and neuroimaging. To analyze MRI, PET and CT scans as well as clinical features like demographic information, cognitive scores and genetic markers, we proposed a model that combines both high end Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with attention mechanisms. This work is a pioneer in this field, and thus more similar evaluation data between our DeepAD-Net model with HNB-PDPA Model or EIDR Model, which will be conducted as future works. This study highlights the promise of merging deep learning approaches with multimodal data to improve early Alzheimer's disease diagnosis. The competitive performance of DeepAD-Net illustrates the potential to improve prediction accuracy and robustness by leveraging state-of-the-art neural network architectures as well as attention mechanisms. Results could be particularly exciting for clinicians using DeepAD-Net as a diagnostic aid and ultimately improving patient management. Going forward, we will continue to refine our model for use with other data sources and in clinical settings related to early diagnosis, as well as management of Alzheimer's disease.

articleTitle: Improving Software Quality Assurance Using a Cross-Context-Attentive Cosine Convolutional Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The software quality determines system performance and reliability. As software systems are becoming increasingly complex, this is an important determinant. Detection of defects at the early stages of the development lifecycle improves software reliability and reduces costs. Traditional Software Defect Prediction (SDP) models suffer from class imbalance, complexity of datasets, and inefficient use of contextual information, which affect the accuracy of their predictions. Therefore, the development of reliable software systems still requires a more robust and efficient defect prediction model. In this manuscript, Improving Software Quality Assurance Using a Cross-Context-Attentive Cosine Convolutional Model (Sox-CNN-XA) is proposed. This study uses the NASA-MDP dataset containing historical records of software defects and various software metrics. Data pre-processing included data cleaning, normalization, and splitting, which was done in order to enhance the quality of the data and make it ready for training and validation purposes. A new framework for Software Defect Prediction (SDP) has been proposed by using the integration of Cosine Convolutional Neural Networks (Cos-CNN) and Cross-Contextual Attention (XCA), which captures spatial and contextual features of data effectively. The hyperparameters in this model have been fine-tuned with Sardine Optimization Algorithm (SOA) in order to get improved performances over diverse datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 99.9%, a true positive rate of 99.9%, and a precision of 99.8% while maintaining a false positive rate of 7.2%. The results clearly prove that the model is performing better than traditional methods. The conclusion shows that the framework can increase the reliability of defect prediction, thus enabling software practitioners to deliver high-quality and maintainable software within tight deadlines and budgets

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Telemedicine: Transforming Remote Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The concept of telemedicine developed before the upsurge of popularisation of telehealth services, particularly with the support of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. This review aims to deeply analyse how these technologies integrate and change telemedicine, improve the diagnostics of diseases, help in the treatment process, and provide more accessible healthcare. Predictive analytics, natural language processing, and tele-therapy monitoring are examples of the ML and A.I. technologies used in patient care management. This is the time of more intelligent and more effective remote care services with the help of several innovative technologies and phenomena like A.I. health chatbots and intelligent treatment algorithms. However, several factors limit its development, including data privacy, legal issues, and users' access to technologies. Directions for further development and continuous healthcare improvement include integrating advanced 5G communication systems and wearables and exploiting blockchain technology for data interchange. These developments create prospects to eliminate current impediments and enhance the provision of healthcare services worldwide. This scope consists of mechanisms for the best present data, emphasizing growth areas of new technologies, especially artificial intelligence and machine learning, that transform healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Urban Traffic Prediction Using Two-Branch Attention Networks With Adversarial Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The prediction of urban traffic forms an essential element in present-day intelligent transportation systems since it assists transportation agencies with improved traffic management and congestion control. Standard forecasting algorithms that monitor traffic experience difficulty in reaching accurate results because urban road networks show complex dynamic characteristics along with weather conditions and incidents on roads. Machine learning and deep learning models experience decreased accuracy when applied to different urban domains primarily due to domain shift problems. This study introduces Adversarial Domain Adaptation Two-Branch Attention Network (ADAT-BAN) as a new solution for urban traffic prediction to overcome existing challenges. The model achieves superior learning process performance through the implementation of the Starling Murmuration Optimization (SMO) algorithm. Optimized traffic parameter selection is achieved through the implementation of hybrid Tasmanian Devil Optimization (TDO) with Zebra Optimization Algorithm (ZOA) to select the most appropriate traffic metrics used for prediction purposes. The solution addresses domain shift problems through effective strategies to identify complex temporal and spatial traffic relationships. The framework achieves exceptional results through experimental testing because it produces prediction accuracy reaching <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 9. 9 \%}$</tex> above existing models. The framework demonstrates high operational capacity toward real-life traffic management in cities through improved urban flow management along with exact predicting capabilities.

Author Keywords: Adversarial Domain Adaptation Two-Branch Attention Network

articleTitle: Marine Sound Classification Using One Dimensional CNN and Fourier Magnitude Spectrum with Optimal Activation Function and Layers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The underwater environment is a complex acoustic habitat, rich in biotic and abiotic sounds. Detecting and classifying these diverse ocean sounds is challenging due to the variability in time-frequency characteristics, amplitude differences, and noise levels. Most deep learning-based marine sound classification is based on the spectrogram, Mel spectrogram, or Mel frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) analysis. The Fourier magnitude spectrum is used as a feature for discriminating animals from ship sounds using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN), which may result in higher accuracy with less computational load. This study aimed to identify the optimal CNN model by developing three architectures with different layer configurations (2, 3, and 4) and evaluating them using four activation functions. The models were trained and tested on the Watkins marine animal sound and ShipsEar databases. Among the activation functions tested, the rectified linear unit (ReLU), the rectified linear unit (threshold 6, ReLU6), the leaky rectified linear unit (LReLU), and the exponential linear unit (ELU), the CNN model with ReLU6 achieved the highest accuracy of 92.13%, specificity of 84.96% and sensitivity of 99.3% demonstrating their classification effectiveness based on the evaluation results. This study also highlights the importance of choosing the right activation function and hyperparameters. Furthermore, the Fourier magnitude spectrum can also differentiate marine animals and ships with high accuracy, less model size, and a lower computational load.

articleTitle: An Optimized YOLO-based License Plate Recognition System with Integrated Privacy Safeguards
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Efficient and accurate license plate recognition (LPR) is crucial for intelligent transportation systems, surveillance, and security applications. This work proposes a Powered Smart License Plate Recognition System utilizing YOLOv8 for real-time detection and Optical Character Recognition (OCR) for character extraction. The system integrates publicly available datasets, including OpenALPR, CCPD, and UFPR-ALPR, along with custom-annotated data to enhance robustness. Data preprocessing involves normalization, augmentation, and privacy protection measures such as Gaussian blurring and encryption to ensure compliance with data protection regulations. The architecture is optimized using convolutional layers for feature extraction and attention mechanisms for improved character recognition. A privacy protection module ensures sensitive information masking, while Edge AI deployment on Jetson Nano or Raspberry Pi enables real-time inference with minimal latency. Model training employs transfer learning with pre-trained YOLOv8 weights, fine-tuned on license plate datasets. Optimizers such as Adam and SGD, along with IoU loss, enhance bounding box accuracy, ensuring precise detection. Performance evaluation demonstrates high mean Average Precision (mAP) exceeding 95% and OCR accuracy surpassing 90%, validating the system's efficiency across diverse environmental conditions. Applications include automated toll collection, traffic monitoring, vehicle tracking, and secure entry management in smart cities. Law enforcement agencies can utilize the system for stolen vehicle identification and traffic rule enforcement. The proposed approach offers a scalable, privacy-aware, and high-accuracy solution for modern LPR applications, ensuring compliance with security and regulatory standards.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Deep Learning Based Fall Detection in Elderly People
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Elderly people are more vulnerable to falls, which can result in serious injuries, a lower quality of life, and higher medical expenses. Traditional fall detection methods, such as wearable sensors or vision-based systems, face limitations in accuracy, comfort, and practicality. Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved fall detection capabilities by leveraging powerful computational models for data analysis and feature extraction. With an emphasis on important methodologies, architectures, and datasets utilized in the area, this paper offers a thorough literature analysis of deep learning-based fall detection strategies. It investigates several deep learning techniques applied to sensor-based and video-based fall detection systems, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and hybrid models. The review also emphasizes the difficulties encountered in practical application, including data privacy and computing cost, and the need for robust datasets. Finally, future research directions are proposed to address current limitations and improve fall detection systems' dependability and effectiveness for elderly care.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Classification Utilizing Modified Probabilistic K-Nearest Neighbor with Active Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Heart disease is a state in which the heart fails to pump sufficient blood to meet the body's needs. It causes approximately 17 million deaths globally each year. Accurate prediction of heart disease is critical for timely intervention and improved patient prognosis. Typically, machine learning methods are widely used for heart disease diagnosis. However, challenges are faced such as sensitivity to correlated features, noise, and imbalanced datasets. To address these limitations, this study proposed a modified probabilistic k-nearest neighbors with active learning (MPKNN-AL) framework. The framework integrates probabilistic modeling for accurate prediction of uncertain data samples. Additionally, metric learning via the markov chain monte carlo (MCMC) scheme is utilized to obtain optimal nearest neighbors, thereby making the framework robust to noisy and correlated features. Further, to overcome the data imbalance and scalability issues, active learning is incorporated to extract the most significant unlabeled instances and add it to the training subset to improve the classification accuracy. This results in a robust and efficient framework for the heart disease classification. Experimental evaluations show that the suggested framework significantly outperforms the baseline methods in accuracy and efficiency, offering a promising solution for the real-time heart disease diagnosis and classification.

articleTitle: A Generative Adversarial Network for Data Augmentation of Ictal Waves from Multi-Electrode Brain Activity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: High-density multi-electrode arrays (HD-MEAs) are sophisticated recording devices used in vitro to capture voltage traces of neural activity. HD-MEAs yield data with a high spatial and temporal resolution at the level of individual neurons. In this study, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were trained on HD-MEA data to classify epileptic seizure waves. A major challenge for the prediction of epileptic seizures was the scarcity of data as ictal waves constitute rare events relative to background neuronal activity. To address this issue, we investigated a method of data augmentation using generative adversarial networks (GANs), a class of deep learning models that are trained to generate plausible synthetic images. We show that synthetic exemplars created by GANs can serve as training data for deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in order to improve classification accuracy. These results suggest a workflow for combining GANs and CNNs in the detection of ictal waves recorded via HD-MEAs.

articleTitle: Multimodal Medical Image Registration Classification Framework Using Squeeze-and-Excitation Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Medical image registration is an essential procedure in medical image analysis. Traditional 2D and 3D registration techniques often face challenges in addressing the intricate variations and conditions found in medical images. Complex deformation issues are commonly encountered in these registration tasks. Although several advanced registration models are developed for registering the medical images. Yet, achieving accurate and efficient deformable registration remains a significant challenge, particularly when dealing with substantial volumetric deformations. Given the difficulties in obtaining ground-truth registration labels, many existing methods utilize an unsupervised multi-modal image registration approach. However, designing effective metrics to assess the similarity of multi-modal images is challenging, which significantly hampers the performance of multi-modal registration. Additionally, due to the differences in contrast various modalities are utilized for collecting the raw images and it becomes a difficult task. Therefore, addressing the numerous challenges associated with traditional multi-modal medical image registration techniques, a novel deep learning approach is designed. Initially, multi-modal image registration and segmentation procedures are performed in this research work. Here, the image registration and segmentation procedure are executed using a UNet-based Autoencoder with Vision Transformer (UNet-A-ViT). Next, the registered and segmented images are provided to the classification phase. In this phase, image classification procedures are performed using Squeeze-and-Excitation Network (SENet) and attain the classified outcomes like malignant and benign tumors. Finally, various experiments are executed in the suggested framework to observe its efficiency over classical techniques.

Author Keywords: Multimodal Medical Image Registration and Segmentation

articleTitle: Next-Gen Waste Management: AI as a Catalyst for Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Traditional waste management techniques frequently be afflicted by inefficiencies, high operational fees, and environmental drawbacks. However, latest improvements in Artificial Intelligence, such as computer vision and Internet of Things, are remodeling waste management right into an automated and optimized procedure. This research study explores how AI-pushed technology enhance waste series, sorting, and recycling methods. Machine learning algorithms enhance waste category accuracy, computer vision permits unique fabric separation, and IoT-powered smart containers optimize collection schedules, decreasing needless trips and gasoline consumption. Additionally, AI-pushed direction optimization algorithms Significantly reduce emissions by means of designing efficient series pathways. These advancements Contribute. Not only to improve operational efficiency but also to the broader dreams of decreasing environmental impact and promoting a Circular economy. Despite its transformative potential, AI integration in waste control affords monetary, ethical, and technological challenges that require cautious attention. This examine provides a comprehensive evaluation of AI packages, their blessings, boundaries, and destiny capacity in revolutionizing waste management. With AI solutions, the enterprise can transition towards a more adaptive, efficient, and sustainable waste management ecosystem, addressing both urban and environmental demanding situations in the process.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Optimizing Electric Vehicle Battery and Navigation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning-based optimization framework for Electic Vehicle that leverages LSTM, CNN, and DRL to enhance battery management, autonomous navigation, and energy efficiency. The LSTM model predicts the State of Charge (SoC) and State of Health (SoH) of the EV battery, utilizing temporal patterns in sensor data to improve predictive maintenance. The CNN-based model focuses on real-time obstacle detection and fault recognition in autonomous driving systems, processing visual data from onboard cameras, LiDAR, and radar sensors. Finally, the DRL model optimizes energy consumption and route planning by training an agent to navigate traffic and road conditions efficiently while minimizing power usage. Data for the system is collected from various sensors embedded in the vehicle, including battery data, traffic information, GPS, and driver behavior. The data is preprocessed and augmented to ensure the models are robust and generalizable. Training involves GPU-accelerated computing platforms to enhance model efficiency. The performance of the models is evaluated through metrics such as R2 score, accuracy, and energy efficiency improvements, with results showing a 20-30% enhancement in energy consumption and battery life. The proposed system has practical applications in battery management, autonomous driving, and real-time energy optimization, contributing to the advancement of intelligent EV technologies. The work presents a step toward integrating deep learning techniques into EVs for improved performance and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Video Deepfake Detection: Current Trends, Methodologies, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Deepfake technology has emerged as a significant challenge in the domain of multimedia processing, particularly due to its capability to create highly realistic manipulated videos that can mislead viewers and compromise security, privacy, and public trust. While deepfake technologies have legitimate applications in fields such as entertainment, education, and healthcare, their misuse for malicious purposes such as misinformation and identity fraud necessitate the development of robust detection methods. This survey provides a comprehensive analysis of the state-of-the-art approaches in deepfake face detection within video data, categorizing them into three major sections: Hybrid Methods, Ensemble Methods, and Recurrent Methods. Hybrid methods integrate multiple machine learning models to enhance the accuracy of spatial and temporal feature extraction, offering a balanced approach to detecting subtle manipulations in deepfake videos. Ensemble methods leverage the combined strengths of diverse classifiers to improve robustness and adaptability in varying video contexts. Recurrent methods utilize recurrent neural networks to capture temporal dependencies across video frames, addressing challenges in detecting complex and sequential manipulations. The review highlights that while these approaches demonstrate significant progress, challenges remain in generalizing detection models to novel and highly advanced deepfake techniques. This work concludes by identifying the limitations in existing research and suggesting future directions for improving the robustness and scalability of deepfake detection systems.

articleTitle: Digital Guardians: Exploring Video Analytics in Autonomous Classroom Surveillance Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The growing prevalence of intelligent surveillance systems has expedited progress in video analytics, particularly in learning environments. This survey article analyzes various methods for assessing student behavior and extracting features from classroom videos, with a focus on identifying test malpractices. We look at many existing systems that use techniques like facial identification, tracking, gesture recognition, and engagement analysis to monitor student activities. Here we shed light on the research needs by showing the benefits and limitations of several strategies that involve coping with occlusions, variable lighting, and small face sections in video frames. Our goal is to develop a strong system that uses live video feeds to detect test malpractices in a better and accurate manner while being efficient.

articleTitle: Fall Detection Using Sound with FPGA Signal Analysis and Machine Learning Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Falls represent a considerable risk to the well-being of geriatric populations, frequently resulting in injuries or mortality. In response to this pressing concern, we introduce an innovative fall detection apparatus employing acoustic sensors and FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) technology to effectively alleviate these hazards. Our system capitalizes on acoustic phenomena, particularly those associated with footstep sounds and falls, which are gathered through routine activities and video documentation to develop a comprehensive model adept at differentiating between fall incidents and non-fall occurrences. The primary attributes encompass the derivation of Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) from the processed auditory signals. To enhance operational efficacy, an FPGA is utilized to execute all data processing functions, inclusive of Fourier transformations and a threshold-based predictive algorithm. This methodology diminishes dependence on conventional computational systems while preserving elevated processing efficiency. The derived features are subsequently employed to formulate a data classification model utilizing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Random Forest Tree (RFT), which proficiently discriminates between sounds indicative of falls and those not related to falls.

articleTitle: Potato Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Potato crops are vital to sustaining global food supplies, yet remain highly vulnerable to diseases for example early blight, late blight, and bacterial wilt which can result in serious yield reductions. Swift identification combined with timely intervention are critical for effective disease administration. In this work, a deep learning based classifier leveraging EfficientNet b0 is introduced for classifying prevalent potato plant pathologies from foliar images, permitting accurate diagnosis and categorization. The proposed model is trained on potato leaf dataset and is able to classify images into healthy, early blight, late blight with a high classification accuracy. If deployed, this work would give farmers and agricultural experts a rapid and scalable solution for crop disease. The study contributes to traditional disease management practices with enriching automated and real-time detection system, diminishing crop losses, and efficacy sustainable agriculture approach. The model has also been validated through experimental studies, which show its potential for use in precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Anomaly and Threat Detection System in Real Time Social Internet of Things using Dimensionality Reduction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The Social Internet-of-Things (SIoT) is an innovative model developing in the struggle to safeguard privacy and increase trust inside the Internet-of-Things(IoT). The revolutionary notion of SIoT combines the IoT with social platforms, allowing inanimate items to develop relationships with one another. The fast growth of SIoT has transformed networked networks, enabling effortless interaction between devices. However, integrating these systems creates major security issues, including anomalies and attacks that may compromise system integrity. This study presents a machine learning(ML) methods like Isolation Forest (IF), One class support vector Machine(SVM) and Kernel density estimation(KDE) for in SIoT networks using the Principal component Analysis(PCA) and Correlation Analysis as dimensionality reduction techniques. The findings shows that the IF method provides an accuracy of 93% with the dimensionality reduction techniques applied on RT-IoT dataset. By utilizing powerful machine learning algorithms and contextual analytics, the framework improves detection accuracy and enables strong device collaboration in highly dynamic contexts..

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks for Accurate Brain Tumor Detection and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Brain tumor detection is a crucial diagnostic process that depends on analyzing MRI images fine contrast of soft tissues and non-intrusive nature. Although through the manual analysis of MRI scans is a time taking process and leads to errors. So, there is a need to develop more accurate, efficient and automated detection systems. This study proposes ResNet (residual network) is one of the efficient models in convolutional neural network (CNN) to detect brain tumors. This paper used an openly available dataset which consists of MRI images (containing and not containing tumors). Then the images are subjected to preprocessing using different types of techniques like data augmentation and normalization to boost the model robustness. ResNet-50 is well known for its specific characteristics like vanishing gradient problem, skip connections was tailored on this dataset. The model accomplished classification accuracy of 95% resembles that this model can classify the brain tumor MRI images efficiently and helps the radiologists for rapid detection of tumors.

articleTitle: PCOS Diagnosis Through Time-Series Analysis Using RNN with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: PCOS is an endocrine disorder commonly seen among women of childbearing age characterized by hormonal imbalance, irregularities in menstruation, and metabolic disorder. Early detection of PCOS helps prevent other complications such as infertility, diabetes, and heart disease. Therefore, the aim of this work is to use an attention mechanism-based RNNs for accurate and interpretable diagnosis. The sequential health data includes hormonal levels and metabolic indicators from which the model identifies patterns leading to PCOS. The mechanism of attention in the model amplifies the critical aspects of time steps, which ultimately enhances the model's performance along with providing more transparency through emphasis on the relevant diagnostic features. The model had a perfect precision, recall, and F1-score of 1.00 when tested with a PCOS dataset, indicating its reliability for transforming gynecological healthcare.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning Systems with Explainable AI: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The convergence of Blockchain with Federated Learning (FL) technology and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) serves as a new framework to solve privacy protection problems, security issues, and interpretability needs. Model training collaborations supported by FL technology allow different entities to develop models while safeguarding raw data from exposure during training processes, thus addressing privacy needs in healthcare and finance. The combined challenges of model vulnerability to malicious attacks, data poisoning vulnerabilities, and explainability issues block broad industrial adoption. Blockchains strengthen FL security systems by providing decentralised solutions that produce unchangeable audit trails through their proof of transparency, immutability, and distributed consensus models. By enabling model interpretability, XAI methods build stakeholder trust and ensure system accountability. The study combines the technologies to analyse current systems and identify gaps that integrated systems should resolve. A detailed review examines explainable blockchain models and privacy preservation methods to tackle performance and implementation limitations within the framework. Combining these technologies builds a transformative process to create secure AI systems that maintain interpretability functions and protect data privacy during system development as researchers develop frameworks for wider application deployment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Real-Time IoT Applications in Cloud Communication Networks Through Adaptive Intelligent Routing and Secure Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The growing Internet of Things network with cloud technology enables real-time solutions in healthcare, autonomous systems, and industrial automation. These systems face challenges with response time, shifting network layouts, power conservation, and data security threats. RPL and traditional routing protocols struggle to adapt to complex networks, while machine learning-based and EERP approaches solve some issues but leave others unresolved. This study presents an AI routing method that enhances live data transfer between IoT systems and cloud platforms. The algorithm tracks network shifts to make fast routing decisions, reducing time delays and conserving power. This study implement basic encryption, device confirmation, and abnormal event recognition to protect data transfers. Simulations compared the technique's performance to RPL and EERP approaches, measuring latency, data delivery rate, energy usage, network speed, and security capabilities. Testing shows a 25-50% improvement in latency and 10-20% better PDR results. Energy utilization decreases by 30-50%, while throughput remains superior. Security features demonstrate reduced encryption overhead with improved anomaly detection and authentication. This research addresses IoT-cloud communication network challenges through an adaptable system that conserves power, protects data, and enhances reliability for time-sensitive applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Healthcare: A Review of Applications, Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This article explores the potential of machine learning (ML) in transforming healthcare. It provides an overview of ML and its various categories, highlighting how supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms can be utilized for tasks like disease diagnosis, treatment personalization, and resource allocation. The article delves into specific applications of ML in healthcare, including image analysis for early disease detection, visualization of complex medical data, and personalized medicine approaches. It further explores the exciting opportunities presented by ML, such as improved diagnostics and treatment, increased efficiency and cost reduction, and advancements in research and development. However, the article also acknowledges the challenges associated with implementing ML in healthcare, including data privacy concerns, real-time data requirements, and the complexity of certain models. Overall, the article emphasizes the multifaceted landscape of ML in healthcare, showcasing its potential to revolutionize the industry while acknowledging the hurdles that need to be addressed for successful integration.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-Transformer for Aerial Object Detection: A Novel Architecture for Enhanced Detection Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Aerial object detection is crucial for applications such as surveillance and environmental monitoring, but challenges such as small object size, complex backgrounds, and variations in scale hinder the performance of traditional models. This paper presents a novel hybrid architecture that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) for enhanced aerial object detection. The model leverages CNNs for spatial feature extraction (using ResNet50) and transformers for global context understanding, aiming to improve both the precision and recall of the detection system. The proposed model is evaluated on the VisDrone dataset and compared with widely used object detection models, YOLOv3 and Faster R-CNN. The results show that the Hybrid CNN-Transformer model outperforms both YOLOv3 and Faster R-CNN, achieving a mAP of 0.45 at IoU 0.5 and 0.33 at IoU 0.75, along with higher Precision (0.58), Recall (0.52), and F1 Score (0.55). These results demonstrate the usefulness of the hybrid approach to avail the improvements in detection accuracy and a better trade-off between Precision and Recall, particularly for challenging aerial images with occlusions and scale variations

articleTitle: ADAS Based Adaptive Lane Detection Algorithm for Curved and Discontinuous Road Markings Using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Over the last few years, autonomous cars have picked up as a means to minimize the prevalence of accidents induced by driver distraction. Intended to increase safety for passengers and optimize traffic conditions, these cars use sophisticated technology for navigation as well as identifying lanes. Existing lane detection has mostly been implemented to detect linear lane markings, but curved as well as non-existent lanes still pose a difficulty. The present research applies MATLAB for detecting lanes in images and videos, including straight, curved, and interrupted lane markings. A camera is installed on the vehicle to obtain real-time road images, which are then processed for the detection of lanes. The Hough Transform method is used to identify lane boundaries by processing through two hyperbolas, making it possible to correctly identify complicated lane patterns. By capitalizing on this method, autonomous cars are able to obtain more accurate lane detection, thus improving overall driving efficiency and safety..

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Networks for Enhancing Soccer Team Performance Through Tactical Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This research investigates using artificial neural networks (ANNs) to improve football team performance via tactical data analysis. The growing amount of data produced during football matches poses challenges and possibilities for coaches and analysts. ANNs, as a category of machine learning, provide a strong foundation for recognizing patterns and extracting actionable insights from data. It created a prediction algorithm that evaluates team performance and recommends ideal tactics using player data, game video, and tactical formations. It indicates that ANNs can proficiently assess intricate relationships inside the game, enhancing coaches' decision-making. The model was also evaluated using past match data, demonstrating its capacity to forecast results and suggesting tactical modifications in real time. This research's ramifications beyond performance improvement players underscore the significance of data-driven methodologies in contemporary sports. This novel use of technology enhances player development and cultivates a profound comprehension of game dynamics, providing a competitive advantage in football.

articleTitle: Automated Ear Infection Detection Deploying Densenet Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Otoscopy is a diagnostic technique that uses an otoscope to look at the eardrum (tympanic membrane) and external auditory canal. With the help of this portable device, which combines a light source and a magnifying lens or camera, medical practitioners may see the eardrum and canal structures. Otoscopy is frequently used to evaluate the health of the ears and find anomalies including infections, inflammation, wax accumulation, foreign objects, tumours, structural flaws, or indications of trauma. For patients experiencing ear-related symptoms such as discomfort, hearing loss, or discharge, it is a crucial step in the assessment process. Otoscopy is usually done as part of a thorough ear examination, and to further evaluate ear function, it may be combined with additional procedures like audiometry or tympanometry. Although otoscopy is essential for identifying a variety of ear conditions, it is still difficult to accurately and quickly classify otoscopy pictures. In this study, we present a deep learningbased automated otoscopy classification system. Thus, we put together a diverse set of otoscopy pictures that included both healthy anatomy and a range of diseases, such as tumours, infections, inflammations, and structural anomalies. For feature extraction and classification, we used Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) using a pre-trained model called the DenseNet framework, a potent family of deep learning models. The model was trained using categorical cross-entropy loss after the dataset had been pre-processed to improve diversity and homogeneity. Common measures including accuracy, precision, recall, F1score, and AUC-ROC were used to assess the model, and hyperparameters were adjusted to maximise performance. Our findings reveal that the suggested method is successful in correctly categorising otoscopy pictures, indicating its potential as a useful clinical tool to support the diagnosis of ear disorders.

articleTitle: Big Data in Social Media: Analyzing Trends, Patterns and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The huge volumes of data produced in social media provide both new possibilities and challenges to analytics. The present paper emphasizes Big Data analytics and Machine Learning (ML) methods to uncover trends, patterns, and user behavior from social media-related data. Such vital concepts, like the “Four Vs” of Big Data: Volume, Velocity, Variety, and Veracity, and innovative tools for datacollection, storage, and preprocessing are covered here as well. Sentiment analysis, trend forecasting, and user behaviormodeling are some of the examples of what is possible using ML and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for deriving actionable insights. Marketing campaigns, crisis communications, and political campaigns are some of the scenarios that are covered to bring out real world applications of such technologies, along with their transformative effects. Lastly, data privacy, quality, and scalability issues are noted, along with ethical concerns and biases. Directions for the future point to developments in real-time data analysis, anonymization, and the changing role of AI in social media platforms. This research emphasizes the significance of Big Data and machine learning in driving innovation and decision-making in the digital era.

articleTitle: Hybrid Routing and Energy Management for Performance Optimization in Mobile Ad-hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Mobile Ad-hoc Networks (MANETs) encounter challenges related to dynamic topologies, energy constraints, and link instability. To enhance performance, a hybrid model integrates Ad-hoc On-demand Multipath Distance Vector (AOMDV), Power-Efficient Gathering in Sensor Information System (PEGASIS), and Deep Q-Network (DQN). OMNeT++, a discrete event simulation framework, facilitates comprehensive data collection, capturing key network parameters such as node density, signal strength, packet transmission rate, residual energy, routing paths, link breakage frequency, and packet delivery status. Stored in scalar and vector files, the dataset enables energy-efficient communication modeling and adaptive routing optimization. Data preprocessing involves cleaning, normalizing, and handling missing values using interpolation techniques while filtering noisy data through a sliding window averaging method. Feature extraction focuses on hop count, queue length, residual energy, and link expiration time, ensuring consistency and facilitating faster convergence. The hybrid model architecture integrates AOMDV for reliable multipath routing, PEGASIS for energy-efficient communication, and DQN for adaptive path optimization. Simulation results indicate a 15% improvement in throughput, a 10% rise in packet delivery ratio, a 20% reduction in end-to-end delay, and a 30% decrease in average energy consumption. Applications extend to military operations, disaster recovery, vehicular networks, IoT sensor networks, and smart city infrastructure, ensuring efficient and adaptive communication.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-LSTM Framework for Accurate Seismic Event Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
