abstract: This study investigates the application of deep learning techniques, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) as well as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, for earthquake prediction using a binary dataset. Predicting Earthquakes is a difficult task because of various factors the complex and non-linear nature of seismic data, and traditional models often fall short in capturing the intricate patterns involved. In this research, a 1D CNN is utilized to automatically extract spatial features from time-series seismic data, effectively reducing the need for manual feature extraction. The CNN is designed to detect local patterns in the data that might indicate upcoming seismic events. Meanwhile, the LSTM element is integrated to capture the temporal addictions as well as long-term trends extant in the seismic signal, given its ability to hold information over prolonged periods. The hybrid CNN-LSTM model aims to predict the occurrence of earthquakes by classifying each instance as either an imminent earthquake (positive class) or no earthquake (negative class) within a specific time frame. The binary nature of the dataset simplifies the prediction task, allowing the model to focus on learning the critical features associated with earthquake precursors. Preliminary results indicate that the integrated CNN-LSTM model is capable of identifying patterns in the data this paper obtained an accuracy of 97% which shows the feasibility of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Cyberbullying Detection Using QDA and LDA Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Detecting cyberbullying is critical in today's digital landscape, where platforms like Twitter, Instagram, and TikTok are integral to communication. These platforms, expose users especially young individuals to harmful interactions, leading to severe consequences such as anxiety, depression, and even self-harm. The anonymity and global reach of the internet often embolden perpetrators, making early detection essential to prevent escalation and ensure community safety. The proposed solution improves upon earlier methods by employing Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) and Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) classifiers, which are effective for smaller, imbalanced datasets. Leveraging preprocessing techniques like stemming, tokenization, and Bag of Words ensures adaptability and efficiency. Unlike computationally intensive models like CNNs, QDA's flexibility and LDA's simplicity balance precision and recall. With accuracies of 81% (QDA) and 79% (LDA), these models provide lightweight, scalable tools for combating harmful online behavior, fostering healthier digital interactions.

articleTitle: Methods for Assessing and Monitoring Anxiety Disorder
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Anxiety Disorder is among the most widespread mental health conditions globally, which requires an innovative approach for efficient monitoring, management and intervention. As one of the promising tools in this domain, wearable technology offers various aspects such as real time monitoring of physiological data and behavioural insights. This survey paper explores the state-of-the-art in wearable devices where detection and monitoring of anxiety disorder is possible with the help of parameters such as ECG, GSR and Actigraphy. These modalities allow continuous monitoring of heart activity, skin conductance and sleep monitoring (movement patterns) which are vital for providing insights on anxiety disorder. This survey aims to help researchers and practitioners with a comprehensive understanding of the potential of wearables in the mental health care field.

articleTitle: MedDrone Rescue: A Survey on Drones for Medical Supplies in Rural, Terrained Areas and Search & Rescue Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Transportation challenges in rural, mountainous, and isolated regions, often due to unreliable infrastructure, hinder the timely delivery of medical supplies and essential resources, especially during crises like natural disasters when swift access is critical. Traditional transport modes are often slow, unreliable, or insufficient in such scenarios, complicating efforts to provide aid. Disaster response teams and rescue organizations face additional obstacles, including rugged terrain, hazardous weather, and logistical constraints, which delay assistance and heighten risks. The adoption of drones, both autonomous and remotely controlled (RC), offers an effective solution. Autonomous drones, equipped with GPS and advanced mapping technologies, can deliver life-saving supplies with precision to hard-to-reach areas, enhancing supply chains for hospitals, NGOs, and under served populations. Meanwhile, RC-controlled drones prove invaluable for reconnaissance and observation, enabling military units, rescue teams, and disaster responders to safely locate victims, assess damage, and gather real-time data in challenging terrains. By leveraging the versatility and efficiency of drones, organizations can overcome logistical barriers, improve access to vital services, and enhance both routine operations and emergency responses, ultimately saving lives.

articleTitle: Real Time Fall Detection Using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Falling is a serious health risk, especially for older adults and patients with some diseases, which often causes long and complicated rehabilitation process after severe injuries. Fall detection system is an important feature that helps users use a device safely and get fast assistance in emergency situations. The proposed project long-story-short is a fall detection system that integrates YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once cc version 8) for object detection with pose estimation and results in a combination of accuracy and performance when identifying falls in real time. YOLOv8 was used due to its fast accuracy for detecting the presence and activity of human and pose estimation algorithm, to track body movements and postures so as to detect abnormal falling patterns. When a fall is detected, the system immediately alerts caregivers or emergency services to ensure a quick response. This work presents a cost-effective, robust, and accurate framework to detect, via falls, and will become more valuable, especially for elderly persons and others with physical challenges. Performance metrics like accuracy, real-time processing speed, and robustness assessed to varied environments to verify its efficacy.

articleTitle: An IoT Based Access Control System Using R307 Optical Biometric Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This work offers the design of an IoT-based access control system using the R307 optical biometric sensor that increases the use of fingerprints for secure access. This system is developed to provide a safe and effective means of securing the restricted areas so adaptable for the different places such as offices, homes, and industries. The hubs of the system are the R307 biometric sensor that scans and verifies the user's fingerprints to unlock the access. The fingerprints are then recorded in the system, only the security personnel they allow access to the facility. This biometric form of identification not only enhances security by rendering door lock and unlocking impossible without the human feature being scanned but also does away with conventional security devices such as keys and cards which are always easy to misplace, copy or even have stolen. The system boasts integration with the IoT, hence its strength due to features such as remote control. Added to that is the provision for attempt log, and in most cases, real-time notifications; thus, the system is portable and expandable. This was especially true for the large-scale scenarios where access points are concurrently utilized. Besides offering highly secure access control models that integrate the fingerprint technology, the system comes with an easily understandable module for enrolling the fingerprints besides other administrative options that allow easy management of the system by both the system administrators and the ordinary users. Apart from this, the IoT framework leaves scope for further development. It is possible to integrate with other security systems or attach new sensors in order to raise the factors for authentication.

articleTitle: Next-Gen AI in Healthcare: Shaping the Future of Precision and Preventive Medicine
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Healthcare professionals benefit from revolutionary changes because of current developments in artificial intelligence technology, which optimise precision medicine and preventive medical practices. Artificial Intelligence technology transitioned from basic rule-based systems into complex deep learning models that accurately analyse intricate medical data over decades. This paper investigates AI's significant influence on healthcare, including diagnostic and treatment operations, current robotics, and automated patient care systems. AI systems assist medical staff by improving precise diagnoses and simplifying treatments while boosting patient supervision through automated intelligence. The advantages of AI medicine simultaneously trigger crucial legal and moral dilemmas about healthcare data security, automated system bias, and AI-developed judgmental processes. The paper examines these issues regarding AI health care deployment while presenting guidelines to establish responsible and equitable use of AI technology in medical applications. The discussion explores how AI will influence genomic research and robotic surgery while demonstrating its potential to transform healthcare practice globally. This paper examines the complete transformation of contemporary medical care through an analysis of AI effects with identified difficulties and forthcoming potential.

articleTitle: Wildeye: Wildlife Surveillance and Alert System using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Wildeye system is a mobile application which enables the surveillance of wildlife providing timely notifications allowing the protection of humans and animals. More security is assured than in an ordinary GIS based system since this mobile application utilizes a more advanced YOLO vision algorithm is a Deep Learning model. The system works in all angles and determines when animals or people are within the camera's field of sight such that notifications are accurate and all the time on time. Alarms were set up and activation triggered by certain events such as when animals are restless, there are changes in the environment such as rainfall Wildeye exercises control on animal activities and people's habits penetrating deepening shocking areas with a goal to manage modern day warfare. Instead of ‘live streaming’, Most of the features are in Wildeye app, except bullets regarding it. For instance, instead of consuming lots of bandwidth in streaming things audible, Wildeye only takes pictures of the detected scenes. Among their functionalities, it also involves shoot detection used as a bid to save the game from poaching. Real time alerts can be scheduled as email alert through SMTP which will then allow him to view the alert on his mobile. But the findings also show, that the degradation of the presented model doesn't suffer much when doing training on the real world images.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Dual Boosting for Alzheimer's Disease Prediction Optimizing Accuracy with Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)

authors.preferredName: V T Ram Pavan Kumar M

abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a difficult task to manage since it is chronic and difficult to diagnose in the initial stages. Forecasting of this diseases progress is very important in terms of treatment and management at the right time. This work presents the 2DB model, a stacked ensemble of AdaBoost and XGBoost classifiers, to improve the accuracy of the AD diagnosis. The dataset adopted includes extensive health, lifestyle, and cognitive factors collected from Kaggle. The work includes an extensive data pre-processing step where issues such as missing values, and normalization, were also tackled alongside SMOTE to deal with the class imbalances. Feature selection is done through Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) to select the relevant predictors. Two-Stage Dual Boosting (2DB) combines the weight distribution of AdaBoost that reassigns weights to all the misclassified instances with XGBoost's gradient boosting method for classification, where logistic regression is the base classifier for meta-classification. The proposed model was assessed with quantitative measurements such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to its maximum accuracy of 94.6%. The performance shows that the proposed Two-Stage Dual Boosting (2DB) model's generalization significantly outperforms traditional classifiers while providing accurate predictions of Alzheimer's disease with better robustness and interpretability. The results of this work show the possibility of increasing the diagnostic accuracy of the junction hybrid machine learning models and have important potential for clinical usage in early diagnosis.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Crop Disease Identification: Comparing CNN and SVM Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Crops form a key part of the food cycle. But, within this vast and complex agriculture domain, the crops have their predators. Crop diseases may cause revenue losses to farmers and jeopardize food security. These detractors, without a doubt, can destroy the productivity and even the quality of crops, creating a definite concern for the economic sustenance of the farmers and food security from a global perspective. The spread of crop diseases has increased in recent decades due to agricultural intensification, globalization, trade, and climate change. For some reasonable circumstances, these farmers do not know the cause of the disease. Thus, there needs to be a valid mechanism through which such farmers can be assisted in diagnosing the crop disease. Henceforth, we have created a machine learning that examines crop leaves to identify agricultural diseases to ease their work. The Implementation of this was done using two algorithms; Convolutional neural Network (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Comparing the two algorithms to determine which is more important for picture categorization is the aim. This study offers a thorough analysis of CNN and SVM algorithms used in agricultural disease detection, with a particular emphasis on fruit and vegetable leaf identification. Using the PlantVillage dataset, it tests these two machine-learning models in multiple implementations. CNN achieved an accuracy of 75.76<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for fruit leaves and 84.38% for vegetable leaves, whereas SVM showed an accuracy of 75.00% for fruit leaves and 75.11% for vegetable leaves. From the above comparison, it can be seen that CNN acts better than SVM, and more so in cases when their feature representations are quite complex. This paper is intended to provide the reader with an overview of how these techniques can best be applied for real-world applications in precision agriculture.

articleTitle: ScaNana: Unlocking Potential Products from Scanned Banana Varieties Using Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The ScaNana project delves into the innovative use of image recognition technology to realize the full potential of scanned banana varieties, with a special focus on Lakatan, Latundan, and Saba. By combining cutting-edge machine learning techniques and practical applications, the project seeks to address pressing challenges in the banana industry. Its primary objective is to develop a user-friendly tool capable of accurately identifying different banana types while recommending a wide array of products that can be made from them. This approach aims to minimize food waste, foster creativity in recipes, and expand bananas' culinary and commercial possibilities. The system employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image classification, leveraging the capabilities of TensorFlow and Teachable Machine for model training. TensorFlow Lite (TFLite) is integrated to enable efficient processing on mobile devices, ensuring that users can access the platform conveniently without needing high-end hardware. Meanwhile, OpenCV enhances image recognition accuracy, making the system reliable and precise. ScaNana aspires to provide an accessible and intuitive platform that allows users to scan bananas, identify their varieties, and explore their potential uses. The project evaluates its functionality, reliability, usability, and efficiency to ensure high performance and user satisfaction. By bridging the gap between technology and sustainability, ScaNana promotes innovation, productivity, and the sustainable use of bananas in culinary arts, product development, and other commercial applications. This initiative champions a greener, more resource-efficient future for the banana industry.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Healthcare: A Review of Current Applications and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has been a main force behind important breakthroughs in patient tracking, personalized medicine, medical tests, and operating efficiency in the healthcare business in recent years. Machine learning algorithms provide unique insights into early disease identification, picture analysis, and prediction analytics, improving diagnosis accuracy and treatment results. These programs are able to examine big and complex information. By predicting treatment effectiveness and genetic risks, machine learning (ML) allows personalized medicine by allowing customized care through tailored therapy approaches. Furthermore, preventative health management is backed by ML-driven prediction analytics and online patient tracking, especially for chronic illnesses. Operationally, machine learning increases process efficiency and cuts costs, allowing for data- driven decision-making and individualized patient care. However, there are important ethics issues with machine learning acceptance in the healthcare business as well, such as data protection, computer bias, and legal problems. This study offers a full analysis of the state-of-the-art machine learning applications in healthcare, stressing their revolutionary potential while discussing the ethics issues and hurdles that must be addressed to ensure execution that is both responsible and fair.

articleTitle: Stomach Cancer Prediction and Detection using Deep Learning: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Stomach cancer, sometimes referred to as gastric cancer, is still one of the most common and widespread deadly disease worldwide offers a significant challenge in oncology due to late detection and high mortality rates. The advent of deep learning has revolutionized stomach cancer prediction by leveraging sophisticated models such as convolutional neural net-works (CNNs), multimodal learning and hybrid frameworks that integrate multiple data sources like medical imaging, histological slides, clinical records and genetic profiles and provide better performance with high accuracy. This review comprehensively ex-plores recent advances in deep learning applications for the detection of stomach cancer, highlighting their performance, accuracy, and clinical implications. Comparative analysis demonstrates that different deep learning models, such as ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNetB5, and MobileNetV2, provide impressive results with accuracy up to 99% and higher sensitivity and specificity. It also indicates that the system accuracy needs to be improved to 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in order to detect stomach cancer as early as possible. Early detection helps in the stoppage of further spreading of the disease and lowers the death rates.

articleTitle: Beyond Playlists: AI-Driven Emotion-Based Music Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Music recommendation systems have evolved from simple playlist curation techniques to sophisticated AI-driven models capable of analyzing human emotions for personalized song suggestions. Emotion-based music recommendation systems integrate advanced machine learning, deep learning, and artificial intelligence techniques to detect users' emotional states through various input modes, including facial expressions, speech tone, text analysis, and physiological signals. These systems aim to enhance user experience by dynamically selecting music that aligns with real-time emotions, thereby improving mood regulation and mental well-being. This review explores the methodologies employed in emotion-based music recommendation systems, including deep learning architectures, facial recognition techniques, and sentiment analysis models. It also discusses the challenges associated with real-time emotion detection, data privacy concerns, cross-cultural differences in music perception, and system adaptability. Furthermore, the paper highlights emerging trends and future research directions, such as multimodal emotion detection, hybrid AI models, reinforcement learning, and ethical AI frameworks. Addressing these challenges and advancements will be crucial in developing more robust, accurate, and user-centric emotion-based music recommendation systems.

articleTitle: CalmNest: IoT and ML Based Smart Cradle Using Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The CalmNest smart cradle addresses the growing need for automated infant care, particularly for working parents who require reliable, responsive monitoring to ensure their baby's comfort and safety. Utilizing an Arduino Nano 33 BLE Sense processor with built-in sensors-including cry detection, environmental monitoring, and proximity sensing-CalmNest automatically responds to the baby's needs. The cradle gently swings when the baby cries, maintains optimal temperature by activating an exhaust fan when needed, and alerts parents to moisture or caregiver presence through Bluetooth-enabled notifications. Developed using platforms like Arduino IDE and Edge Impulse, CalmNest achieves a 92.6% cry detection accuracy, with additional enhancements for stability in temperature and humidity monitoring through a DHT11 sensor and OLED display. Performance analysis confirms that CalmNest successfully balances automated comfort and safety, creating a smart parenting solution that reduces manual intervention and supports a secure, nurturing environment for the baby. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Plant Leaf Disease Detection Using EfficientNet Asynchronous Propagation Penalized Neural Network with Planet Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Unpredictability in illumination conditions, similar illness symptoms, skewed datasets, processing expense, and the challenge of determining infections at their onset are some of the challenges in plant leaf disease diagnosis. Model accuracy, reliability, and generalization across different types of plant species are also influenced by environmental factors, occlusions, and image noise. Using PlantVillage database, this paper confirms the superiority of the EfficientNet Asynchronous Propagation Penalized Neural Network with Planet Optimization Algorithm (ENet-APPNNet-POA) in plant leaf disease detection. Image quality is initially enhanced by the Adaptive Tri-Plateau Limit Tri-Histogram Algorithm (ATP-LTH) approach. ENet-UNet (EfficientNet-based U-Net) divides the affected areas of plant leaves according to distinct regions. Asynchronous Propagation Penalized Neural Network (APPNNet) serves as the classifier responsible for extracting features before performing their category identification. The Planet Optimization Algorithm (POA) delivers improved results and accuracy in classifying plant leaf diseases by evaluating various classifications affecting different leaf areas. PlantVillage dataset is employed in the Python test script. Test results indicate that ENet-APPNNet-POA outperforms existing methods to detect plant leaf disease classes at 99.9% efficiency and 99.8% sensitivity, an indication that computerized systems are likely to supersede manual diagnosis.

articleTitle: An Improved Design of ResNet for Plant Diseases Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This paper presents a new application of deep convolutional neural networks for automatic plant disease clas sification, which is one of the key challenges to sustainable agriculture and food security globally. Herein, we have used a residual network with nine layers utilizing residual learning to overcome the vanishing gradient problem in deep networks. It was trained on a dataset containing 70,295 images from 14 plant species, each affected by 26 different diseases, also involving healthy specimens. The resent state-of-the-art deep learning techniques are: batch normalization, adaptive learning rate scheduling with the One Cycle policy, Adam optimization, and 25 epochs of training with GPU. In order to make the performance evaluation robust, we applied a rigorous cross validation strategy. The results are very outstanding in efficacy, with validation accuracy reaching 99.25% and validation loss as low as 0.0220. Compared with most benchmarks available in pathology image classification literature related to plants, this performance is far better. Our results have proven that deep learning has huge potential in phytopathology, specifically for non-invasive high-throughput early detection of diseases.

articleTitle: Optimized Machine Learning Framework for Liver Disease Prediction Using Ensemble Learning and Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The detection of liver disease at early stages remains vital because this disease causes considerable health impacts worldwide. Biomedical liver function tests and clinical assessments used for diagnosis require extensive time. The authors suggest a novel machine learning framework that implements ensemble learning together with automated feature selection to predict liver diseases. Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) constitute the set of classifiers which integrate into a Voting Classifier (Random Forest + XGBoost + LightGBM). The proposed method reaches performance levels of 89.8% accuracy and 89.5% F1-score together with 89.2% recall. ROC-AUC analysis demonstrates high sensitivity and specificity levels of this method which indicates its applicability for clinical usage. The proposed model surpasses former approaches leading to 7-10% better accuracy rates in evaluation tests.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Patient Monitoring in Smart Hospitals: A Survey on Edge Computing Integration and Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and edge computing in healthcare is transforming patient monitoring systems, particularly within smart hospitals. These technologies enable real-time data processing, enhanced decision-making, and improved patient outcomes by shifting computational tasks closer to data sources, reducing latency, and alleviating the burden on centralized cloud infrastructures. This survey paper provides a comprehensive review of the current state of AI-driven patient monitoring systems in smart hospitals, focusing on the role of edge computing. It explores key applications, such as vital sign monitoring, early disease detection, and predictive analytics, while highlighting the benefits of edge computing, including real-time analytics, enhanced data privacy, and resource efficiency. Furthermore, the paper examines challenges in the deployment of AI and edge computing in clinical settings, such as data security, interoperability, scalability, and the need for robust AI algorithms tailored to healthcare environments. The survey concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential advancements to further enhance AI-driven patient monitoring systems in smart hospitals. This review serves as a valuable resource for researchers and healthcare professionals aiming to understand the intersection of AI and edge computing in modern healthcare infrastructures.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS): Challenges, Benefits, Applications, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: AI-based Clinical Decision Support Systems are a revolutionary innovation in the healthcare sector, using artificial intelligence to improve diagnostic precision, optimize treatment planning, and enhance patient outcomes. This paper discusses the challenges, benefits, applications, and future directions of AI-driven CDSS. Some of the key challenges are data quality, integration with EHRs, ethical concerns, and explainability issues. Despite these challenges, benefits such as efficiency improvements, reduced clinician workload, and the possibility of tailored medicine are substantial. In addition, the paper depicts diverse applications across oncology, cardiology, and primary care. The paper further stresses the directions: validation of robustness, user-friendly interfaces, and equitable deployment to achieve maximal utilization of AI-CDSS in global health care systems. Besides this, the integration of multimodal data and improvement in predictive analytics will help to revolutionize preventive care. Moreover, ethical practices with AI will bring forth trust and adoption. Such an all-inclusive review signifies the pivotal role AI will play in shaping clinical decision-making for the future.

articleTitle: Designing and Analyzing Green Networking Solutions in Data Centers Using AI for Energy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: A significant obstacle in the world of information IT, especially in terms of energy efficiency, is the increasing demand for energy from data centers. These massive plants currently consume nearly 1% of the world's electricity, and this percentage is expected to increase significantly in the coming decades. Therefore, it has now become imperative to identify effective ways to maximize the energy use of data centers, which has led to the study of the use of artificial intelligence to come up with creative solutions. The purpose of this research is to use AI to optimize energy use in data centers by designing and analyzing green networking solutions. It entails using AI methods like neural networks and reinforcement learning to increase data centers' energy efficiency and lessen their environmental effect. The study specifically focuses on enhancing important characteristics, including cooling systems and Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). This study aims to replace conventional, static energy management techniques with adaptive strategies that react to current facts and anticipated energy demands by utilizing artificial intelligence. It is anticipated that the suggested solutions will significantly increase energy efficiency, lessen their negative effects on the environment, and help data centers become more sustainable.

articleTitle: Developing and Comparing Protocols for Low-Latency IoT Networking
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance comparison study of MQTT and CoAP protocols of IoT that ensures low latency. The main motivation is to illustrate the performance, as well as limitations, of these protocols concerning key performance indicators that include latency, power consumption, and reliability. The work makes theoretical analysis while also conducting hands-on experiments on the test-bed environment, including tools for the simulation of real-world scenario software such as Wireshark and Python. The results show that CoAP is more suitable for applications that require minimum latency, while MQTT provides better reliability in message delivery. Finally, the research points out that appropriate protocol selection concerning specific application requirements is of paramount importance; this is a foundational step toward the development of more efficient IoT communication strategies for future innovations.

articleTitle: Intelligent Crop Yield Modeling Using Attention Networks and Dynamic Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Improvement in Farm Yield Projection is a step toward addressing the increasing demand for food production globally. This depends on several factors, including environmental conditions (temperature, rainfall, humidity), management practices (irrigation, fertilizer use), genetic variations (crop variety), and regional aspects (soil type, climatic zones). Capturing the complex relationships between these features is necessary to create an accurate predictive model. This study suggests a dynamic predictive model that can account for non-linear interactions that affect yield. Attention neural networks are used to capture the nonlinear relationships between features. A dynamic ensemble classifier is developed utilizing these interactions and features using dynamic weights to choose the base learner. The model is further optimized for edge device deployment through lightweight architecture pruning. Additionally, a comprehensive ablation study validates the significance of attention mechanisms in improving predictive performance. Experimental results on a real-world dataset from Maharashtra, India show a 12.5 % improvement in accuracy over baseline models. The proposed framework is adaptable for multi-region, multi-crop applications, supporting precision agriculture and sustainable farming practices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sweet Corn Leaf Disease Detection with Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Sweet corn (Zea mays saccharata), a crop vital to both global food security and economic sustainability, is particularly susceptible to diseases such as northern corn leaf rot and maize smut. large output losses, putting agricultural productivity at risk. Since the existing methods of diagnosing illnesses rely on manual examinations, which are often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to errors, there is an urgent need for improved diagnostic approaches. The AI-powered system in this study uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to analyze photos and identify sweet corn illnesses. The suggested CNN model was trained using a sizable number of carefully gathered, previously processed photos of sweet corn leaves. The model outperformed conventional methods with remarkable performance indicators such as 92.5% accuracy, 93.0% precision, and 91.0% recall. Through encouraging sustainable farming methods, lowering crop losses, and aiding in early disease detection, artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to radically revolutionize the agriculture industry. In order to significantly improve detection accuracy and operational efficiency, future research will try to integrate real-time monitoring technologies, such as drones and Internet of Things-based systems. This study emphasizes how critical it is to use cutting-edge technologies to solve pressing issues in contemporary agriculture.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Resolution Enhancement Framework for Low-Resolution Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: A crucial task in computer vision is image super-resolution (SR), which aims to improve the quality and resolution of low-resolution images. The Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) and the Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network (SRCNN), two well-known deep learning techniques for super-resolution images, are thoroughly analyzed and compared in this research. SRCNN is a novel data-driven technique that optimizes the end-to-end mapping function by employing convolutional neural networks to directly map low-resolution images to their high-resolution equivalents. SRGAN, on the other hand, combines adversarial training with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to produce high-resolution images that are perceptually realistic, improving both visual quality and resolution to meet human standards. The study examines the differences in SRCNN's architecture, training techniques, and output features, highlighting the system's simplicity and effectiveness.

articleTitle: InterACT: Enhancing Human-AI Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models and computer vision systems has opened new frontiers in artificial intelligence. This paper introduces InterACT, a novel cross-modal system that integrates leading language and vision models to enable more intuitive and context-aware human AI interactions. By leveraging the strengths of both modalities, InterACT processes natural language queries to guide object detection in visual environments, bridging the gap between linguistic and visual understanding. We evaluate the performance of three language models of varying sizes in conjunction with an advanced object detection model, exploring the balance between computational efficiency and interaction quality. Our experiments demonstrate InterACT's potential across diverse real-world scenarios, revealing promising results in maintaining contextual relevance and adaptability. This research contributes to the growing field of cross-modal AI systems and lays the groundwork for more sophisticated human AI interactions, with implications for applications ranging from assistive technologies to educational tools.

articleTitle: Federated Transfer Learning for Early Detection of Multi-Organ Failure: A Scalable Predictive Healthcare Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The early Identification of multi-organ disorder (MOF) is critical for improving patient results in critical care settings. This paper presents a novel predictive healthcare framework depends on Federated Transfer based Learning (FTL), designed in addressing the challenges of early MOF detection over multiple organs, including the heart, liver, kidney, and lungs. By utilizing federated learning, the proposed model leveraged decentralized patient information from diverse medical institutions while ensuring data's privacy and security. Transfer learning will be employed to enhance model accuracy by transferring knowledge from pretrained models over similar medical domains. The scalable framework will be optimized for real-time analysis, giving robust predictions that assisting healthcare professionals for timely decision-making. The Extensive experiments using real-world medical datasets shows the model's superior performances in terms of prediction accuracy level, sensitivity rate, and generalizability. This research highlighted the potential of FTL to revolutionize predictive healthcare by enabling collaborative, data-privacy preserving, and scalable solutions for MOF identification.

articleTitle: Approaches for Summarization of Articles Across Multiple Languages: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Multilingual text summarization requires efficient solutions because global content continues to increase in quantity. The paper provides an overview of contemporary field advancements that derive from the fundamental literature. Advanced scoring models and transformer models alongside domain-specific pretrained models demonstrate notable success with their implementations. Content extraction has benefited from PageRank-based approaches and word embedding techniques and new datasets have enabled abstraction summarization in languages including Malayalam and Hindi. The combination of rules with neural networks produces effective solutions for domains such as biomedical fields and legal document aggregation. New knowledge-enabled transformers expand summarization capacities through integration between discourse relations and entity-awareness capabilities. Progress has been made in managing language diversity, but the field continues to encounter difficulties with preserving semantic value and the cultural basis of underrepresented languages. The analyzed research indicates that achieving breakthroughs requires specialized datasets together with strong evaluation tools and model-based innovations that address ongoing challenges. The evaluation demonstrates how multilingual summary technology enables better accessibility across educational settings and journalism fields and social media platforms. This study develops multilingual summary technology by conducting state-of-the-art methodological investigations and identifying existing research gaps within global information inclusivity.

articleTitle: A Review on AI - Enhanced Security in Blockchain and Cloud-Based Electronic Healthcare Records Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The combination of Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and cloud computing have the potential to significantly improve the security and use of Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) systems. This study looks into the future possibilities for AI-enhanced security and Predictive Analytics in Blockchain and Cloud-based EHR systems. Blockchain technology provides dependable solutions for data integrity, privacy, and safe sharing, whilst cloud platforms offer scalable and readily available infrastructure. AI improves these systems by providing improved threat identification, anomaly detection, and real-time automated responses, hence strengthening the security architecture. Furthermore, AI-powered Predictive Analytics in Cloud-based EHR systems enables early identification, personalized treatment, and improved patient outcomes. As the healthcare sector faces rising cyber dangers and data management challenges, merging these technologies is crucial to developing strong, efficient, and patient-centric EHR systems. However, combining AI with Blockchain presents ethical concerns, regulatory compliance hurdles, and the need for interoperable systems. This paper looks at current advancements and emerging developments in safe and predictive healthcare data management, such as quantum-resistant algorithms, federated learning, and AI-powered smart contracts. Continued research and innovation are necessary to fully fulfill these technologies potential for transforming healthcare delivery.

articleTitle: IoT and the Future of Healthcare: Revolutionizing Remote Patient Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) transforms the healthcare service into innovative avenues of remote patient monitoring (RPM), monitoring real-time trends about patients outside a traditional clinic environment. Herein, a case is described, focusing attention on the power of IoT while enabling RPM - data collection and transfer, transmitted in real time across several health-generating devices or instruments, such as wearable sensors, and home-monitoring systems, as well. RPM has proven itself to be the most effective in the management of chronic diseases, fewer hospital visits, and improved outcomes for patients by continuous and tailored care. Challenges in data privacy, device interoperability, and regulatory compliance continue to persist, although the transformative power of RPM lies in its ability to further change healthcare in more proactive, accessible, and efficient manners by leveraging breakthroughs like AI and 5G. This paper identifies the advantages, disadvantages, and future possibilities of IoT in RPM and places critical emphasis on the future shaping of patient-centered care.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Navigation Using Waterwheel Plant Algorithm for Coordinating Smart Grids and Intelligent Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The efficient charging of electric vehicles (EVs) remains essential to create sustainable mobility while EVs transform into crucial elements of upcoming transportation systems. The present EV charging navigation systems deal with three main issues including grid congestion and inadequate charging station (CS) selection and delays from traffic conditions.This paper proposes a novel Waterwheel Plant Algorithm (WWPA) for optimizing EV charging navigation within the Smart Grid (SG) and Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). The suggested method strives to enhance SG-EV coordination through demand balancing in addition to charge price reduction and decreased grid congestion levels. WWPA algorithm serves as the proposed method to optimize EV charging schedules. The MATLAB platform serves as the implementation environment for the proposed method which demonstrates superior performance than Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), Coati-Northern Goshawk Optimization (Coati-NGO) and Grey Sail Fish Optimization (GSFO). Results demonstrate that the WWPA algorithm reduces average charging expenses by 18.14% throughout diverse charging operations as it produces superior performance than existing algorithms operating in the SG ITS.

articleTitle: A Location and QR Code-Based Solution for Efficient Attendance Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This study makes the case that consistent attendance is essential for students' achievement and that conventional approaches to managing attendance might be ineffective and time-consuming for educators and administrators. According to the proposed approach, a computer-based attendance management system that uses location and randomized QR codes may be a useful way to deal with issue. The methodology employed in the development of the system is based upon two distinct perspectives., the user perspective, which pertains to the web application utilized by the students, and the administrative perspective, which concerns the web-based administration system employed by the instructor. This method involves a two-step attendance management system. The process begins with authorized faculty members generating and sharing a dynamic QR code with students. Students then scan the QR code, system verifies both the QR code value and the student's location. ensuring accurate attendance by cross-checking the scanned QR code and student's real-time GPS coordinates to confirm their presence within the class room. The integration of QR code scanning with location validation provides a robust solution for managing and verifying student attendance in an efficient and secure manner.

articleTitle: Advancing Healthcare Through Internet of Things: A Comprehensive Review of Smart Healthcare Systems and Their Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has turned the healthcare domain in a better direction due to more interconnected and smarter systems that enhance care delivery. Certainly, the IoT-accessible applications in these fields are only possible if devices, sensors, and real-time data are interconnected. Among today's marvels are remote patient monitoring, wearable health trackers, telemedicine, and smart hospital management. Medicine gets more personal, effective, and accessible due to these improvements. However, its development remains unmatched being faced with complexities such as security of personalized data, safety risks resolution, and seamless device-to-system integration. This paper examines the influential role of IoT in advanced healthcare systems, with its virtues, major applications, and implementation obstacles as the subject. The Internet of Things as a mode of health and technology bridging can entirely change how medicines are being practiced and even lead to the improvement of the lives of patients by introducing adaptive and efficient hospital systems. Thus, IoT can be a technology that balances tech and medicine for the betterment of patient treatment outcomes and make the system adaptive and efficient.

articleTitle: Big Data Analytics for Credit Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: This project focuses on utilizing big data analytics in the banking sector to aid in decision-making processes, particularly in assessing the creditworthiness of loan applicants. By employing machine learning algorithms such as Decision Trees and Random Forests, the project aims to develop predictive models to identify trustworthy customers, thereby minimizing financial risks for banks. Python, PySpark, and Jupyter Notebook are utilized for data preprocessing, analysis, and model development. The project workflow involves data cleaning, exploration analysis, model building, and evaluation. Banks can make data-driven decisions to optimize their loan approval processes through this approach.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-based Framework for Accurate Loan Prediction: Comparative Insights With Traditional Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The primary goal of this study is to develop a new approach to loan prediction using Support Vector Machines (SVM) and comprehensive statistical analysis. Improving forecast accuracy and laying a solid foundation for loan eligibility determination are the goals of this undertaking. The goal of this project is to improve the reliability of loan prediction models by leveraging statistical insights and Support Vector Machines (SVMs). The results and borrower profiles were culled from a dataset of loans. After some preliminary processing, we used the Random Forest as a foundation and added a custom Support Vector Machine (SVM). To improve precision, models were trained, performance metrics were examined, and statistical analysis was carried out. The implementation was carried out using Python with scikit-learn and TensorFlow, which guaranteed the preservation of ethical data management practices. The outcome was a statistically significant improvement in loan forecast accuracy between the Random Forest Algorithm and the new Support Vector Machines (SVM). When it comes to forecasting the amount of the loan that the consumer received, the Randomforest algorithm obtains a level of accuracy of 78.86%. A score of 70.73% was achieved by Support Vector Machines (SVM), so this is a significant improvement.

articleTitle: Low Budget Solar Infrastructure for House as Substitute of Grid Electricity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: In this article, as an alternative to grid electricity, the solar-based electricity generation approach has been proposed to assist middle-class households because even today, a large portion of the world's population is either deprived of electricity or encounters massive electricity outages. To install a longlasting solar system, although a standard financial investment is required, it can provide enough benefits compared to grid electricity to the consumers, basically to the lower-income families. However, when buying a solar system, customers are not always aware of the pricing background as well as module specifications, which not only increases overall installation cost but also restricts electricity production. Considering this fact, in this work, we have developed low-budget configurations of solar infrastructure to help economically weak people. In this work, we have systematically discussed which solar system will be better for the people, including the price of small and medium solar systems, and provided a proper guideline for modules' specifications and installation. Results demonstrate that our proposed solar infrastructure is highly efficient for user requirements and can be a substitute for the grid system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of AI Models for Accurate Early Diabetes Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Diabetes is a common long-term disease with significant health implications, necessitating early and accurate diagnosis to manage and mitigate its impact. The use of deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) algorithms is investigated in this study to predict diabetes based on patient-specific factors, including medical history and lifestyle habits. By leveraging various algorithms, the research evaluates and compares their prediction accuracy to identify the most effective model. The findings aim to improve the early detection of diabetes, providing insights into the performance and feasibility of AI-driven diagnostic approaches in healthcare. In the experimental study we have compared machine learning and deep learning algorithms with the same dataset and found that convolutional neural network outperformed other algorithms.

articleTitle: Advancing Cardiovascular Disease Prediction Using LLMs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The heart is perhaps one of the most vital organs supporting human life, but it is more at risk in our contemporary world with its rapid pace of life. The lifestyles in modem times and exert an immense burden on cardiovascular health. All these factors have led to a growing rate of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) across age groups and turned heart disease into a predominant cause of death globally and an emergent public health issue. One of the most urgent challenges in the fight against heart disease is the challenge of obtaining timely diagnosis. Most people only get to know about critical cardiovascular diseases after they suffer from life-threatening incidents like heart attacks or associated complications. The delay is usually a result of the insidious and deceptive presentation of initial symptoms, which are often misunderstood as insignificant health issues. For example, breathlessness can be due to stress or exertion, whereas blackouts can be confused with dehydration or fatigue. But such innocuous-sounding symptoms can be a harbinger of severe cardiovascular illness. Early detection and treatment are the key to preventing the advancement of heart disease and lowering the risk of sudden, disastrous cardiac events. Without timely and correct diagnosis, life-saving treatment windows are lost, and severe consequences become more likely. Raising awareness and enhancing diagnostic techniques are thus the critical first steps in confronting the global cardiovascular health emergency.

articleTitle: MRI Brain Tumor Classification Using Optimized APSO-LLRBFNN
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: The research presents a new efficient machine learning method to classify brain tumors because this task remains vital in fighting the high incidence of brain cancers. The proposed approach unites all its operations including image segmentation with feature extraction and classification into a single processing system. This study uses Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Adaptive PSO (APSO) methodologies to optimize Locally Linear Radial Basis Function Neural Network (LLRBFNN) resulting in PSO-LLRBFNN and APSO-LLRBFNN model implementations. The research examined the optimized APSO-LLRBFNN models against Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Least Mean Squares (LMS) based LLRBFNN classifier methods. Results from experiments show that APSO-LLRBFNN gives superior outcomes with 98.93% accuracy and takes 12.23 seconds for execution, which surpasses currently available methods.

articleTitle: Brain Tumour Identification Using MRI Images: Classification and Optimization Based Random-Coupled Neural Network with Cat Hunting Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Tumors in the brains may be Benign or malignant but they are growths of cells in the brain. Aches, seizures, vomiting, dementia, and impaired vision are generic symptoms of the ailment. In early diagnosis, detection of the disease and determining the right treatment method for the patients MRI scans are important. There are a number of Deep Learning-based detection techniques available, however their accuracy and error rates may be low. This study uses a Random-Coupled Neural Network with Cat Hunting Optimization (RCNNet-CHOpt) to identify and classify brain tumor in order to get around these issues. Only one kind of BraTS dataset is used by the suggested approach: The filters to enhance image quality and reduce noise, the input images are pre-processed using the Adaptive and Propagated Mesh Filtering (APMF). This is followed by feature extraction and classification using Mellin Transform (M-Trans) with Random-Coupled Neural Network (R-CNN). When combined, these two networks can accurately classify the images and identify important elements. Finally, to increase accuracy, the weight parameter of R-CNN is modified using the Cat Hunting Optimization (CHO) technique. The proposed method has a 99.8% recall and a 99.9% accuracy rate, outperforming existing methods. Among the primary advantages of the RCNNet-CHOpt are decreased false-positive rates and enhanced precision in identifying intricate brain tumor formations. Hence, it is an especially useful tool for clinical use in the identification of brain tumor because most of these applications manage large volumes of medical data.
